exclude: the second screen of the double-buffered display (display_flip shows $4400 and $4800 in turn); while a stage loads the fast loader's copy of $BD00-$C0FF runs here, and is counted at $BD00
10 parts: Ending, Level 1.1, Level 2.1 and others
elsewhere: 10 parts: Ending, Level 1.1, Level 2.1 and others

comments.text: Object table, one byte for each of the 15 objects (cleared when an object dies). Before the first stage starts the first bytes hold the BASIC line of the game file's loader ("SYS 5632"), which nothing reads.

The KERNAL's vectors, $0300-$0333, as the KERNAL left them. The engine changes the IRQ vector $0314 (irq_install) and the NMI vector $0318 (start); the KERNAL reaches the rest through its own routines.
KERNAL IRQ vector, low byte; irq_install points it at irq_entry.
KERNAL IRQ vector, high byte.
KERNAL NMI vector; start sets its low byte to $C1, pointing it at the RTI at $FEC1 in the KERNAL ROM.
Music-on flag: music_frame runs the player only while it is set; music_init sets it and music_stop clears it.

Music player, one tick per frame for the three voices. A speed counter ($0898 against $0897) decides on which frames the voices read new commands; a global filter sweep adds $08B4/$08B5 to the shadow cutoff $095A/$095B every frame. For each voice (X = 2 down to 0, SID register offset from $093B) it reads two-byte commands at the voice's data pointer ($0938/$0935): a first byte below $25 picks a command from the jump table at $095E/$0983 (the JSR at $03CD is rewritten to point at it), with the second byte in A; otherwise the voice's note timer, effects (portamento $0765, vibrato $06A0, waveform choice, arpeggio $0671, pulse sweep $061B) and gate are updated in the shadow registers at $0945.
Operand of the JSR at $03CD: the address of the music command handler, written from the jump tables each time a command is read.
Operand of the CPX at $0455: where music_update's voice loop stops. 0 plays all three voices (music_hooks_all); music_hooks_ingame sets 2, so that only the third voice is played during a level.
Counts down the current note's length ($0932/$08E7, a 16-bit count per voice); near the end it clears the gate bit in the voice's shadow control register, and at zero it falls into music_next_note.

Starts the next note of a voice: clears the voice's effect counters, reloads ADSR and pulse width from the voice's instrument settings ($090B, $0902, $0908), reads the note byte (zero is a rest), converts it with music_note_freq (adding the transpose and an optional second interval for arpeggio), stores the frequency in the shadow registers and the voice's state, then reads the length byte. A note byte of $19 takes a further length byte.

Starts the tune whose header $FC/$FD points at. Clears the player's 155 bytes of state ($0896-$0930), gives each voice a release point of 2, a note length of 1 and a vibrato period of 1, and sets the tempo $0897 to 1. Keeps the header address in $093E/$093F as the base for section calls. Voice 1's data starts right after the four-byte header; the header holds two 16-bit offsets, relative to that point, for voices 2 and 3. Then silences the shadow registers, runs two ticks and sets the music-on flag $0334.
Clears the music-on flag $0334, then (entered at $058E) clears the 24 shadow SID registers $0945-$095C and the volume register $D418.
Clears the shadow SID registers $0945-$095C and the SID's volume and filter register.
Music command: repeat a section. Counts the voice's loop counter ($0911,X) up; until it reaches the count in A, jumps the data pointer back to the address saved by music_cmd_loop_mark.

Music command: mark the start of a repeated section, saving the voice's data pointer in $0917/$091D and clearing its loop counter. $05CA and $05D2 are the same pair of commands for a second, nested loop level (offset by three voices).

Music commands that each store A into one voice setting: $05D8 transpose ($08F9), $05DC note release point ($08AE, or $08A5 above 99), $05EA waveform choice ($08AB, or the voice whose notes drive the filter, $0896, above 98), $05F8 pulse sweep limits ($08F3 high nibble, $08F6 low nibble), $0607 vibrato period ($092F), $060B filter resonance and routing ($095C), $060F filter start ($08B6), $0613 adds A to the volume and filter mode ($095D).
Sweeps a voice's pulse width (shadow $0947/$0948) up and down by the step in $090E between the limits held in $08F3 and $08F6, turning at each.
Music command: sets the voice's control (waveform and gate) byte $0905.
Arpeggio, mode 1: on alternate frames ($08E1 bit 0) puts the note's second frequency ($08BA/$08BD) or its own frequency into the shadow registers.
Vibrato: after a delay ($08C9), moves the frequency up or down by the depth $08C6 each frame through music_freq_up/down, changing direction every $092F frames in a four-step cycle ($08ED).

Music commands that store A into a setting: $06D8 arpeggio interval ($08D5), $06DC filter sweep step (high five bits to $08B5, low three to $08B4), $06EA tempo ($0897), $06EE second-note interval ($08D2), $06F2 adds A to the transpose ($08F9), $06FA vibrato delay ($08CC).
Music command: return from a called section, restoring the data pointer saved by music_cmd_call ($0923/$0929) and the outer saved one.
Music command: fine tune added to every note's frequency ($08E4).
Adds the vibrato depth $08C6 to the voice's 16-bit frequency ($0899/$089C) and writes it to the shadow registers; $0730 subtracts it.
Subtracts the vibrato depth from the voice's frequency and writes it to the shadow registers (the other half of music_freq_up).
Converts a note number (bits 0-6, plus the voice's transpose $08F9) to a SID frequency from the table at $09A8, adds the fine tune $08E4, and returns it in A (low) and Y (high).
Music command: high byte of the portamento step ($08FF); $088E sets the low byte ($08FC).

Portamento: mode 1 glides the frequency towards the target note ($08BA/$08BD) from either side and stops on it, mode 3 glides down, mode 2 (never reached in the recorded play) glides up. Steps are $08FC/$08FF.
Music command: pulse-width sweep step ($090E).
Moves the voice's data pointer $FC/$FD on by one two-byte command.
Starts a tune: Y and X are the low and high bytes of its header. Turns the player off while music_init sets it up.

Music commands that store A into one voice setting: $0810 portamento delay ($08C0), $0814 vibrato depth ($08C6), $0818 portamento mode ($08B7), $081C arpeggio mode ($08A8), $0820 note gap ($08B1), $0824 attack/decay ($090B), $0828 volume and filter mode ($095D), $0867 sustain/release ($0902), $0892 pulse width high byte ($0908).
Music command: sets the attack and decay of the voice's notes ($090B).
Music command: converts A to a frequency and makes it the portamento target ($08BD/$08BA).

Music command: call a section. Saves the return pointer (two levels, $0923/$0929 and $0926/$092C), then jumps the voice's data pointer to the tune base plus the 16-bit offset given by A and the next byte.
Music command: end of tune. Stops the music and drops the player's two return addresses, so the frame's update ends there.
Called every frame from the interrupt: when the music-on flag $0334 is set, runs music_update and copies the 25 shadow registers $0945-$095D to the SID at $D400-$D418.
Runs music_update and copies the shadow registers to the SID, without checking the music-on flag (music_init calls it twice).
Operand of the LDY at $087B: the first shadow register music_frame copies to the SID ($18, counting down).

Operand of the CPY at $0886: the shadow register below which copying stops. 0 copies down to $D400 (all voices); during a level it is $0E, so only the third voice's and the filter and volume registers are written.
RTS of the last command handler. music_init addresses $0895,Y with Y from 155 down to 1, so this is the base of the state it clears ($0896-$0930), not a target of its own.
The voice (0-2) whose every new note restarts the filter sweep: the cutoff is reset from $08B6 when that voice starts a note. Set by a music command ($05EA, values above 98).
Tempo: the number of frames between the frames on which the voices read new commands.
Frame counter for the tempo; the voices read commands on the frame it wraps to zero.
Current frequency of each voice, low byte (three bytes, one per voice; the high bytes are at $089C).
Current frequency of each voice, high byte.
The note each voice is playing (zero for a rest).
Each voice's control byte (waveform and gate) for the current note, copied from $0905 when the note starts.
Release point of each voice: when the note's remaining length (low byte, high byte zero) falls below it, the gate bit is cleared.
Arpeggio mode of each voice (0 off); see music_arpeggio.

Attack waveform of each voice: 0 none, 1-5 a control byte from music_waveforms used for the first frames of each note ($08AE frames), then the note's own control byte. Values of 6 and more take the path at $0400, which no recorded tune reached.
Number of frames the attack waveform lasts at the start of each note (0: the whole note).
Frames per step of the arpeggio and the three-step cycle of each voice.
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's low three bits each frame (set with $08B5 by music command $06DC).
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's high byte each frame, with the carry from $08B4.
Filter cutoff (high byte) that the sweep restarts from on each note of the filter voice.

Portamento mode of each voice: 0 off, 1 glide to the target note, 2 up, 3 down (three bytes; $08B8 and $08B9 are the second and third voice's, also written by music_init's header loop through $08B8,X).
Portamento target frequency of each voice, low byte; music_init's header loop also stores through $08BB,X (X from $7E) into the voice pointers.
Portamento target frequency of each voice, high byte.
Frames after the start of a note before the portamento starts.
Frames since the voice's current note started (cleared at each note, counted each tick); compared with the portamento delay and the attack length.
Vibrato depth of each voice: the frequency step per frame (0 off).
Vibrato delay counter of each voice, reloaded from $08CC at each note.
Vibrato delay of each voice, in frames.
A counter of each voice stepping 0, 1, 2 every $08B1 frames, cleared at each note.
Glide interval of each voice: when not zero, each note glides towards the note this many semitones away (music_cmd_porta_target).
Arpeggio interval of each voice, the semitones of the second note (the code that uses it, at $04D0, is not reached in the recorded tunes).
Frame counter of each voice towards the next arpeggio step ($08B1).
Arpeggio step counter of each voice; bit 0 picks which of the two frequencies plays.
Fine tune of each voice, added to every note's frequency.
Remaining length of the voice's note, high byte ($FF before the first note); the low byte is at $0932.
Vibrato frame counter of each voice, towards a change of direction every $092F frames.
Vibrato phase of each voice, a four-step cycle (up, down, down, up).
Pulse sweep direction of each voice.
Pulse sweep upper limit of each voice.
Pulse sweep lower limit of each voice.
Transpose of each voice, in semitones.
Portamento step of each voice, low byte.
Portamento step of each voice, high byte.
Sustain and release of each voice's notes.
Control byte (waveform) of each voice's notes, copied into the note at its start.
Pulse width (high byte) of each voice's notes.
Attack and decay of each voice's notes.
Pulse sweep step of each voice (0 off).
Repeat counters of each voice, two levels ($0911 and $0914).
Saved data pointer (low bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Saved data pointer (high bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections, two levels.
Second-level return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Second-level return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Vibrato period of each voice: frames between changes of direction.
Remaining length of the voice's note, low byte (high byte $08E7).
Data pointer of each voice, high byte.
Data pointer of each voice, low byte.
SID register offsets of the three voices: 0, 7 and 14.
Address of the tune's header (low $093E, high $093F), the base for section calls.
High byte of the tune base; also the base of the waveform table, which music_update indexes as $093F,Y with Y from 1 to 5 (the table proper starts at $0940).
Control bytes chosen by a voice's waveform setting 1-5: pulse ($41), sawtooth ($21), triangle ($11), noise ($81), pulse and triangle ($51).
Shadow copy of the SID registers $D400-$D418, written by the player and copied out by music_frame each frame.
Shadow of voice 1's frequency high byte; with Y = 0, 7 or 14, the same register of each voice ($D401, $D408, $D40F).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, low byte (indexed by the voice's register offset).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, high byte.
Shadow of the voice's control register (waveform and gate).
Shadow of the voice's attack and decay.
Shadow of the voice's sustain and release; $0952 and $0959 are the second and third voices' (the shadow continues to $095D).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, low three bits ($D415).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, high byte ($D416).
Shadow of the filter resonance and voice routing ($D417).
Shadow of the filter mode and volume ($D418).
Low bytes of the 37 music command handlers, indexed by the command number minus one; the high bytes follow at $0983.
High bytes of the 37 music command handlers (see music_cmd_lo).
SID frequencies of 96 notes, eight octaves from C-0 ($0116) to B-7 ($F810), two bytes each, low byte first.

Sound effects, one tick per frame for three channels (Y = 2 down to 0, channel state at offsets 0, $1D and $3A of $0C1A): counts down each effect's length, sweeps its frequency and pulse width between limits, and every $0C2C frames switches between the effect's two sets of SID values; ends the effect and clears its priority ($125D) when the length runs out.
Operand of the LDY at $0A68: the number of the highest sound effect channel, 2 (three channels) or 1 when the in-game music has the third voice (sound_set_music_mode).
Operand of the LDY at $0A91: the channel being updated, saved by sfx_update at $0A6A.

One sound effect channel's tick (X = state offset, $FF = SID voice offset): length countdown, frequency sweep up, down or bouncing between two limits ($0C2B bits 0-3), second frequency sweep ($0C2B bits 4-7), pulse sweep, then writes frequency, pulse and control to the SID voice from one of the two parameter sets.
Operand of the LDA at $0B55: the frequency (high byte) at which a sweep restarts, written from the limits at $0B35.
Operand of the LDA at $0BC5: the restart frequency of the second sweep, written at $0BA5.

Sound effect channels' state, three blocks of 29 bytes ($0C1A, $0C37, $0C54), one per channel. The first 20 bytes are copied from the effect's definition by sfx_start: attack/decay, sustain/release, then the fields named below; the rest is working state. In the file as loaded these bytes hold leftover assembler text ("...HEX 5C5D5EB0...").
Sound effect channel: sustain and release (definition byte 1).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's lower limit, high byte (definition byte 2).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's upper limit, high byte (byte 3).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's sweep step, low byte (byte 4).
Sound effect channel: first frequency's sweep step, high byte (byte 5).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's pulse width, high byte (byte 6); lowered by the pulse sweep.
Sound effect channel: flags (byte 7). Bit 0 sweeps the pulse width down by $0C27 each frame, bit 3 alternates between the two parameter sets every $0C2C frames.
Sound effect channel: second frequency's lower limit, high byte (byte 8).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's upper limit, high byte (byte 9).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's sweep step, low byte (byte 10).
Sound effect channel: second frequency's sweep step, high byte (byte 11).
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's pulse width, high byte (byte 12).
Sound effect channel: pulse sweep step (byte 13).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's control byte (waveform and gate, byte 14).
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's control byte (byte 15).
Sound effect channel: length, low byte (byte 16); counted down each frame.

Sound effect channel: sweep modes (byte 17). Bits 0-1: first frequency still, up (1) or down (2 or 3); bits 2-3 what happens at the limit: 0 stop, 4 restart from the other limit, otherwise turn round. Bits 4-7: the same for the second frequency.
Sound effect channel: frames between switches of parameter set (byte 18).
Sound effect channel: length, high byte (byte 19); the effect ends when it passes zero.
Sound effect channel: first frequency, low byte (working state).
Sound effect channel: first frequency, high byte.
Sound effect channel: second frequency, low byte.
Sound effect channel: second frequency, high byte.
Sound effect channel: 1 while an effect plays.
Sound effect channel: which parameter set is playing (0 or 1).
Sound effect channel: first parameter set's pulse width, low byte.
Sound effect channel: second parameter set's pulse width, low byte.
Sound effect channel: frames left before the next switch of parameter set.
SID register offset of each sound effect channel's voice: 0, 7, 14.
Offset of each channel's state block in sfx_state: 0, $1D, $3A.
Offset of the last definition byte in each channel's state block ($13, $30, $4D); sfx_start copies the definition backwards from there.
Two bytes of $FF before the effect address table; nothing reads them.
Addresses of the 30 sound effect definitions, two bytes each, low byte first; each definition is 20 bytes from $0D62.
High bytes of the sound effect definitions' addresses (the table is read as words from $0C7C).
Clears the SID's voice registers, the six sound effect request bytes $1260-$1265, and sets the volume to 15.

Starts sound effect Y on channel X: copies its 20-byte definition (sfx_defs) into the channel's state, gates the SID voice off, sets attack, decay, sustain and release, and the starting frequencies of both parameter sets.
Operand of the LDA at $0CE8: the address of the definition sfx_start is copying, written from sfx_defs.
Operand of the LDY at $0CF3: the channel number sfx_start was given, saved at $0CD0.
The 30 sound effect definitions, 20 bytes each: attack/decay, sustain/release, frequency limits and steps, pulse values, control bytes, sweep modes, length and switching period.
Sustain and release of sound effect 7, which stage_start sets to $FF.
Sound effect 29's first sweep step, low byte, rewritten by $CEEB and changed each time by $CF17.
Sound effect 29's first sweep step, high byte, rewritten by $CEEB and counted down by $CF21.
70 bytes between the last sound effect definition and the start-up code at $1000 that nothing in the engine reads: assembler leftovers in the file as loaded.

The engine's first instruction after the game file is loaded. Calls init_hardware ($3656), switches the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out ($01 = $35), sets the low byte of the KERNAL's NMI vector $0318 to $C1 (so that with the KERNAL in, an NMI ends at the RTI at $FEC1 and RESTORE does nothing), calls $CF2F, clears new_game_flag, sets CIA 1 port A as output and port B as input for the keyboard, and jumps to game_restart.

Starts at most one requested sound effect per call: the first of the three channels whose request flag ($1260-$1262) is set has its flag cleared and the effect number in $1263-$1265 started by sfx_start. When the in-game music is on, the third channel's check at $1041 is overwritten with RTS (sound_set_music_mode), so effects then use two channels.

Requests sound effect X (0-28). Looks up its channel ($FF86,X), priority ($FFA3,X) and effect definition ($FFC0,X); if the priority is at least the channel's current one ($125D,Y), it takes the channel: stores the priority, the effect number in $1263,Y and sets the request flag $1260,Y for sfx_play_pending.
Clears the extended colour mode bit (bit 6) of $D011.
Turns all sprites off and sets the extended colour mode bit (bit 6) of $D011; vic_ecm_off clears it again. Called before the screen is redrawn.
Clears the horizontal fine scroll in $D016 and returns. No instruction in the engine refers to it.
Sets $D016 to 40 columns with no horizontal fine scroll, keeping the multicolour bit.

Installs the raster interrupt chain. A is the memory configuration for $01; X and Y are the first raster routine's address, written into the JSR at $1105. Masks both CIAs' interrupts. With carry set the handler is irq_entry_rom_off at $10F2, which saves the registers itself (the KERNAL is banked out), otherwise $10F8, reached through the KERNAL's vector at $0314; it is written to both $0314 and $FFFE. Enables the raster interrupt at line $F9, stops CIA 1 timer A and enables interrupts.

Raster interrupt handler. Entered at $10F2 (pushes A, X and Y itself) or $10F8 (registers already pushed by the KERNAL). On a raster interrupt it acknowledges it and calls the current raster routine (operand at $1106); the routine returns the next interrupt's raster line in A and the next routine's address in X (low) and Y (high), which are stored for the next interrupt. Leaves through the KERNAL's register restore at $EA7E, or through irq_exit at $115C after irq_use_own_exit.
Sets the border and background colours to black.
Fills colour RAM $D800-$DBE7 with A and both screens, $4400-$47E7 and $4800-$4BE7, with the character code in X (the stores are rewritten with the values each call).

Makes irq_install end the interrupt handler with irq_exit ($115C) instead of the KERNAL's $EA7E, by rewriting the two immediate operands at $10CA and $10CF; irq_use_kernal_exit at $1162 puts $EA7E back.
Restores Y, X and A from the stack and returns from the interrupt.
Puts the KERNAL's interrupt exit $EA7E back into irq_install (see irq_use_own_exit).
Disables interrupts and banks the ROMs out, leaving RAM and I/O ($01 = $35).

Raster routine for the bottom of the screen: switches the display to 24 rows while the beam is past the 24-row border line, waits for raster line 0 and switches back to 25 rows, so the VIC never starts the upper and lower borders. Returns no next routine of its own; it is reached through the raster chain's address table.
Reads joystick port 1 ($DC01) into the five flags $1277-$127B, like joy2_read. No instruction in the engine refers to it.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) into five flags, one per direction: $127C up, $127D down, $127E left, $127F right, $1280 fire. A flag is zero while its switch is closed (pressed). The masks are written into the AND at $11BE.
Selects keyboard rows with A on CIA 1 port A, then reads port B until two reads agree and returns it in A.
Low bytes of the start addresses of the 25 rows of the screen at $4400; screen_row_hi at $11F3 holds the high bytes.
High bytes of the start addresses of the 25 screen rows at $4400 ($44-$47).

Tests the 15 objects against a box and calls a handler for each that is inside it. The box is $3B/$3C (the lowest and highest y, against $C260,Y) and $3F/$40 (the x limits, against $C25F,Y), with $44, $45 and $42 saying where it lies against x position 256: each object's ninth x bit is in $C25B, five objects to a byte, read with the byte $3A and the bit $3E. Objects that are dying (state 4 or more), switched off ($023C, $C23D), of type $37 or showing the blank sprite $0F are skipped; an object in state 3 is tested whatever its other flags. A double-height sprite ($C006) gets a second test 15 lines lower. A hit jumps to the handler written at $13CE with the object index in X. In a torture chamber ($126C set) only object 0 is tested.

Starts the death of object X: unless it is already dying (state 4), sets its state, clears $C0FF and $C10E and, for an object showing the blank sprite $0F that is not of type $37, only scores (score_add). Otherwise it gives the object its death type (the low nibble of $C441, through object_set_type) and the death colour cycle named by the high nibble (level tables $8E02, $8E11 and $8E20), scores it, restarts its movement, switches it to its death movements ($C2D9 for x, $C2E8 for y, from the level tables at $8E2F/$8E4F and $8E6F/$8E8F) and makes its sprite multicolour ($C000). Killing the level's end creature (slot $8F0C) within three of the level's end ($8B95) starts the stage-complete countdown $1266 at 60.

The number of levels started in this game: 0 until the first game, zeroed by game_new and raised by one by level_begin each time a level starts (1 in level 1.1, 2 in level 1.2, up to 6 in level 3.2, the last torture chamber and the ending). loading_setup gives it to load_route_colour, which paints that many steps of the route on the loading map.
Sets the stage number $12A2 to $FF and falls into stage_next, which takes it to 0: the stage that loads the file 1@ and then the first level.

Starts the next stage: stores X in $14D0, banks the ROMs out, adds one to the stage number $12A2, silences the sound, fills the stack page with $FF, clears zero page from $02 up and jumps to the loading screen at stage_load ($F7CB).

What stage_next was given in X: 1 after the last life, 0 for anything else (a completed stage, a quit, a new start). It survives the load: loader_hand_over ($BE31, run at $4931 in the copy) adds a life and enters the stage when it is 0, and enters the attract block at $E503, where the high-score check runs, when it is 1.

Opens the stage's file on drive 8 through the KERNAL, with the BASIC ROM out and the KERNAL in ($01 = $36). Before the first level (stage 1) it goes straight to the KERNAL calls; otherwise it first prints "LOADING:" (print_at string 12) in the bottom rows and the stage's progress bar from the stage tables at $BF46 and $BF51, with characters built at $5001. Sends the two-character file name ($BF39) with LISTEN and OPEN, then TALK, and reads the first byte. If the drive reports file not found ($90 bit 1 after the read), it asks for the other side of the disk (insert_side_prompt). Otherwise it jumps to the fast loader at $4800.

Prints "INSERT SIDE B AND" and "PRESS FIRE TO START" (print_at strings 13 and 14) in the bottom rows, colours the bottom row, waits for the fire button to be pressed and released, pauses about a third of a second and tries the file again at $14E7.
Set once fire has been pressed in insert_side_prompt, so that a held button is not taken twice.
34 bytes of assembler leftovers before the graphics at $1600; nothing refers to them.
50 NOP instructions and an RTS: a delay. The attract's opening scene calls it twice at $EE93 to time its raster split once the logo is falling.
Three NOPs and an RTS: a delay the attract's line-by-line loop calls at $E8D8.

Resets Clyde's weapons for a new game: the selection $12A5 to 0 and the count owned $12A6 to 1, $CFE2 to 1, owned_weapons to the first weapon alone (frame $57, then the $FF end), all three tablet icons to it, their positions (tablet_icons_place), and the panel's weapon icon (weapon_icon_draw with 0).
Chooses the first weapon (position 0, weapon 0: $1A94 and $1A96 cleared) and sets it up (weapon_setup with X and Y 0). Called at each new game and by add_weapon_fallthrough.

Starts a new game: chooses the first weapon (weapon_select_first), sets the stage number $12A2 to 1, zeroes route_progress, clears the score $B7E4-$B7E7, resets Clyde's weapons (player_reset), sets $CFED to 2, clears the potion counts potions_total-$B8A2, sets the eight bytes $B419-$B420 to $FF and $CFE3-$CFEA to 0 and then makes the first of each 1, and sets the lives $B7BF to 4. Then it runs on into level_begin.

The tail of game_new, also called on its own by the witch's shop ($ECAE) as each later level starts: clears the scroll position $1273 and level section $1274, adds one to route_progress, clears the 20 items-taken bytes from $B96B, resets the stage timer ($ACA6), copies the level's five hook addresses from $8CE8-$8CF1 into the engine's calls at $1CB9, $2C32, $2D76, $2E88 and $1BA6, and jumps to $1D7A.
Stores A, X and Y into $0456, $087C and $0887 (operands inside the music player).

X = 0 for sound effects only, 1 for the in-game music. Sets the number of effect channels (the LDY at $0A68, from $12B5,X: 3 channels or 2) and the opcode at $1041 (from $CEDB,X: LDA or RTS) so that with the music on, effects leave the third voice alone.
Calls music_set_hooks with A = 2, X = $18, Y = $0E.

Starts a level after its file has loaded. Resets the stack, blanks the screen, disables the VIC's interrupts, fills the screen with character $FE, silences the sound and clears zero page $0B-$10 and the object position tables ($C25F-$C27C, $C14A-$C167). Points the IRQ vector at $22E8 and the NMI vector at $22E7, banks the ROMs out, masks the CIA interrupts, calls $CEEB, enables the raster interrupt, calls $3D4A, sets the first interrupt at line $FF, multicolour 40 columns, stops CIA 1 timer A and calls $CF2F. Sets $126D-$1272 to $FF, restores the panel's bytes $2532-$2541 and $2562-$2569 from their copies and enables interrupts. Then clears the variables $120C-$126C, sets up the opening, plays two effects (numbers $15 and $16), and runs the opening loop at $19FB: one pass per frame, until the scroll position $1273 reaches $FF.

The opening's frame loop: waits for the frame flag $120D, then on frames counted by $120E calls $26ED, scrolls $1FC2, updates the eight sprite slots ($1FC6, $1CE1, $1CF3), on alternate frames calls $1D95, counts down the panel timers $2562-$2569 and the bytes $2532-$2541 with the flags in $2519, and updates the sound effects. Leaves when $1273 reaches $FF.

Sets up play after the opening: selects the music mode from $12B4, for the first two stages calls $CF9D and the level's $A9E2, calls $3102, sets the player's start position and sprite colours, sets the sprite pointers of both screens, and starts the level's tune (address at $8D56/$8D57) when the music option $12B4 is on.

The in-game frame loop. Waits for the frame flag $120D, then (unless $123D freezes the game) runs the slow tick $26ED, the scroll, the player ($1F83 or $1E0E and $B3C0 while dying, $2F0A), the level's own routine (hook at $1BA6, while $122B is set), the enemies ($31CA, $2E82, $2A14) and the object updates ($C45F, $C764, $C826), then the sound effects. Continues at $1BD2.
JSR whose operand ($1BA6) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CF0.

Second part of the frame. With the music option on, starts the level's end tune once the scroll position comes within three of the level's length ($8B95), unless already started ($1217), and runs the music player (music_frame) except while $125A or $123D hold it. Then, unless the game is frozen ($123D) or skipping a frame ($1210): $3C2C, the level's routine ($ACB6 in a torture chamber, $1214) or the two player-shot updates ($3DFC with X = 0 and 2), the sprite multiplexer's sort ($1FC6), the status panel ($B71E), pending score ($B840 when $B808 is set) and the panel colours ($1D8B).

End of the frame. Clears the skip flag $1210 and steps the frame-divider bits (frame_divider). While paused ($123D), Q (keyboard row $7F, bit 6) quits through game_end with X = 0. Counts down the stage-complete delay $1266 and on zero goes to the next stage. When the player's energy $1288 is zero, takes a life ($B7BF): with lives left it calls level_section_from_scroll and restarts at the section ($3663); with none it ends the game through game_end with X = 1. Otherwise calls $AC9D and the level's per-frame routine (operand at $1CB9) and loops to game_frame.

Stage-complete countdown: decrements $1266 each frame and, when it reaches zero, starts the next stage (stage_next with X = 0). object_kill sets it to 60 when the level's end creature dies near the end of the scroll.
Takes a life: decrements the lives counter $B7BF. The C64-Wiki's POKE 7328,208 (unlimited lives) replaces this instruction's opcode.
JSR whose operand ($1CB9) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CE8: the level's own routine, called every frame.

Ends the game (X = 1 after the last life) or quits it (X = 0, Q while paused). Silences the SID. On stage 1, with the attract block still at $E000, jumps straight to its $E503 (X = 1) or $E500. From any later stage it sets the stage number to $FF and goes to stage_next with X, which loads the file 1@ and level 1.1 again; loader_hand_over then enters the attract block the same way.
Operand of the LDX at $1CD7: the X that game_end was called with.

Steps the four flags $1219-$121C as the bits of a counter: $1219 changes every call, $121A every second, $121B every fourth and $121C every eighth, so routines can run on every second, fourth or eighth frame.

Moves the 15 objects left with the scrolling. For each object that is dying (state 5) or active ($023C), it counts down $C22E (setting $C23D when it runs out), then subtracts the scroll speed ($1DE5, or nothing for objects whose $C39C bit 7 is clear and that move on their own) from the object's horizontal position $C25F (two bytes per object), flipping the object's bit in the position high bits $C25D/$C25C on a borrow.
The horizontal step for this object: Y (the scroll speed) is written into the SBC at $1D55.
Operand of the LDY at $1D4F: the object index, stored at $1D13 so that Y can be reloaded after the step is chosen.
Operand of the SBC at $1D55: the step the object moves left this frame.
Operand of the LDA at $1D5C: the position high-bit byte of the current group of objects ($C25D, then $C25C), decremented after each group of eight.
Operand of the STA at $1D61, kept equal to $1D5D.
Sets the level section $1274 to the first entry of the level's section table ($8C23) that is not below the scroll position $1273: the section the player restarts in after losing a life.
Calls panel_colours on frames where both $1219 and $121A are set (every fourth frame).

Animates the status panel's sprites: steps $1211 through 8 colours (table $1DE7 into the colours of panel sprites 2 and 3 at $254C and $254D, $1DEF into the colour at $25CF set by the lower panel routine) and $1212 through 15 steps (table $1DC7 into panel sprite 7's pointer at $2549, $1DD6 into its colour at $2551).
15 sprite pointers ($B8-$BB) cycled into panel sprite 7 by panel_colours, an animation of the panel icon.
15 colours cycled into panel sprite 7 with panel_cycle_a.
Pixels the landscape scrolls each frame; $1DE6 holds the normal value restored after the weapons tablet.
8 colour values cycled into $254C and $254D by panel_colours.
8 colour values cycled into $25CF by panel_colours.
Sets the tablet's closing countdown $12A4 to 11 frames and the zero-page bytes $53-$56 for it, and clears $24F0.

The weapons tablet, while it is shown ($124A bit 7). Reads the joystick. Fire released (bit set again) selects the weapon in the middle: calls $B44B and tablet_close_setup, sets $124C and closes the tablet through tablet_close. With fire held, left or right starts a turn of the carousel: over six steps the three weapon icons (sprite positions in the panel code at $2572-$257D) slide by two pixels a frame, the one leaving is moved to the other end, the selection $12A5 moves through the list of owned weapons at $2592 ($12A6 of them), and sound effect 0 plays at each step.
Requests sound effect request 0 (sfx_request with X = 0).
Returns in X the index before the selected weapon $12A5, wrapping to the last of the $12A6 owned weapons.
Clears the three sound effect channels' priorities $125D-$125F.

Counts down $12A4 while the tablet closes ($2B1E each frame), then clears the tablet flags $124A and $124C, sets $24F0 to $FF, frees the effect channels, takes the chosen weapon from the list ($2592 at the selection, minus $57) into $1A94 and its list position into $1A96, restores the scroll speed (unless in a torture chamber) and sets the weapon up through $3102.
Three bytes counted down by the first frame loops ($1A1D, $1B28) by the scroll speed, until they reach 0 or $FE.
RTS: an empty routine.

Spawns the level's objects as the landscape scrolls. $1FC2 counts the scroll distance to the next spawn record; when it reaches zero (or was $FF) the record at $1FC3/$1FC4 is read. Each record is 17 bytes. Byte 0: the object slot (low nibble) and the x movement it takes when it dies (high nibble, $C2D9). Bytes 1 and 2: its x and y movement scripts (bits 0-5, through the level's tables at $8E2F/$8E4F and $8E6F/$8E8F), their top bits together choosing a delay from $8ECF for $C351. Byte 3: its type (bits 0-5), which gives its animation script ($8D5A/$8D92, the first byte its first sprite frame in $C16A) and animation speed ($8DCA), and two flags ($C3BA). Byte 4: its colour, a fixed colour below $10, otherwise a colour cycle (list address from $8E02/$8E11, delay from $8E20). Bytes 5 and 6: its position. Byte 7: what a hit does ($C1D4), which also decides whether its movements and animation run freely or only when it is hit; bit 6 makes its sprite double height ($C006). Byte 8: multicolour (bit 0, $C000) and behind the landscape (bit 1, $C003), scroll flags ($C39C), a linked group (bits 4-6, $C3AB) and bit 7 ($C1E3). Byte 9: hit points ($8EAF) and a lifetime ($8EBF). Byte 10: score value (low nibble, $C17A) and the y movement it takes when it dies. Byte 11: its death type and death colour cycle ($C441). Bytes 12-14: the x movement, y movement and type a hit can switch it to ($C2F7, $C306, $C315); or, with $FF, byte 13 names a flag in $B96B that stops it spawning once set (an item already taken); or, with $FE, it rides on the object in slot byte 13 at the offsets byte 14 gives ($C450). Byte 15: hits needed to trigger its behaviour ($8EDF) and $C0FF. Byte 16: the distance to the next record. The slot's other tables are cleared, the object is made active, its ninth x bit set ($C25B: objects enter at the right) and the pointer moves on 17 bytes.
Operand of the SBC at $1FE3: 1 when the spawn counter had passed below zero ($FF), else 0.
Operand of the ORA at $2054: the colour-table group from byte 1's top two bits, combined with byte 2's.
Operand of the LDA at $2082 (two bytes, $2083/$2084): the address of the object's movement script, whose first byte is read into $C16A.
Operand of the LDA at $20B7 (low byte; $20B9 holds the high byte): the address of the colour-cycle list chosen by record byte 4, whose first entry becomes the object's colour in $C11D.
High byte of the LDA operand at $20B7, written from the level table at $8E11: with $20B8 it points at the colour-cycle list whose first colour the spawned object starts with.
Operand of the LDA at $225D: 0 or 1 from bit 0 of record byte 8, choosing whether the object joins collision group $C000.
Operand of the LDA at $2273: from bit 1 of record byte 8, whether the object joins collision group $C003.
Operand of the LDA at $2289: from bit 6 of record byte 7, whether the object joins collision group $C006.

Splits an object slot X (0-14) into a group Y (0-2) and a position X (0-4) within it. The objects are drawn in three bands of five on sprites 3-7, so their sprite attribute bytes ($C000, $C003, $C006, $C25B) hold five objects to a byte, at the bits $BF77+X ($08-$80).
Raster routine prologue: saves A, X and Y in $0C-$0E and acknowledges the raster interrupt.
Six NOPs, a short delay, falling into irq_next.
Sets the next raster interrupt: line A, handler X (low) and Y (high) in the vector at $FFFE.
Restores A, X and Y from $0C-$0E and returns from the interrupt.
RTI: the NMI vector points here during play, so RESTORE does nothing.
The first raster routine of a level (stage_start points the vector here, line $FF): chains to raster_top at line 0, waits through the NOP slide, then joins the scroll update at irq_scroll.

Fine scroll, once a frame: subtracts the frame's scroll amount (operand at $22FB) from the fine scroll $10 (0-7); when it passes a character it moves the VSP column $0F on (0-40, then wrapping, with $120F reset to 39) and raises the coarse-scroll request $120E. Raises the frame flag $120D when the scroll amount is 8.
Operand of the SBC at $22FA: the pixels the landscape scrolls this frame (0 while paused).

Raster line 0: chains to raster_vsp_prepare at line $2F, runs $C00D (the sprite multiplexer's first band) and sets the first band's background colours ($D021-$D023 from $12C9, $12BD, $12C3, each only when not negative).

Raster line $2F: saves A, X and Y into the operands at $23C3-$23C7 and the stack pointer at $23BB, points the next interrupt at raster_vsp on line $30 and enables interrupts inside the handler, then runs the NOP slide so that the next interrupt arrives on a known cycle.

Raster line $30, entered on an exact cycle: points the next interrupt at raster_band2 (line $51), sets the fine scroll in $D016, enters the NOP slide at $1808 plus half the VSP column $0F (one more cycle for an odd column) and then writes $12 and $1B to $D011. The delay decides how many characters late the VIC starts fetching the screen, so the playfield scrolls sideways without characters being copied (VSP). Restores the stack pointer, sets $D018 (operand at $23BE: which of the two screens is shown) and the saved registers, and returns.
Operand of the LDA at $23BD: the value for $D018, choosing the screen at $4400 or $4800 (flipped by $2785) with the character set.

Raster line $51: chains to raster_band3 at $71, sets the second band's background colours ($12CA, $12BE, $12C4) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $23EE, from the level's band table via $26BE).
Operand of the JSR at $23ED: the sprite multiplexer routine for band 2, chosen by level_band_routines.
Raster line $71: chains to raster_band4 at $91, sets the third band's colours ($12CB, $12BF, $12C5) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $2418).
Operand of the JSR at $2417: band 3's sprite routine.
Raster line $91: chains to raster_band5 at $B1, sets the fourth band's colours ($12CC, $12C0, $12C6) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $2442).
Operand of the JSR at $2441: band 4's sprite routine.
Raster line $B1: chains to raster_band6 at $D1, sets the fifth band's colours ($12CD, $12C1, $12C7) and calls the band's sprite routine (operand at $246C).
Operand of the JSR at $246B: band 5's sprite routine.

Raster line $D1: chains to raster_panel_low at $E3, sets the sixth band's colours ($12CE, $12C2, $12C8), clears the sprite priorities and sets up the status panel's sprites: the weapons tablet's (panel_sprites_tablet) while it is open ($124A), else the score panel's (panel_sprites).

Sets all eight sprites for the weapons tablet: positions from $2572-$2581, pointers from $2582 (both screens' pointer bytes) and colours from $258A; multicolour for sprites 0, 1 and 5-7, no expansion.

Sets all eight sprites for the score panel: positions from $2532-$2541, pointers from $2542 and colours from $254A; multicolour for sprites 6 and 7, sprites 5 and 7 beyond x 255, sprites 0-5 expanded sideways.
Operand of the LDA at $24EF: $FF normally; panel_sprites thus enables all eight sprites. tablet_close_setup clears it, and raster_bottom then takes a shorter delay.
Score panel sprite positions, x and y for each of the eight sprites; restored from $2552 at each stage start and moved by the opening's countdowns.
Score panel sprite pointers, one per sprite.
Score panel sprite colours, one per sprite (some animated by panel_colours).
The panel sprites' starting positions, copied to $2532 at each stage start.
Eight countdowns used by the stage opening ($19FB) to slide the panel sprites into place; restored from $256A at each stage start.
Starting values of the eight panel countdowns.
Weapons tablet sprite positions, x and y for eight sprites; the three icon positions at $2576-$257D slide when the tablet turns.
Weapons tablet sprite pointers; $2582-$2584 are the three weapon icons shown.
Weapons tablet sprite colours.
The weapons the player owns, as sprite pointers ($57 upwards, one per weapon), ended by $FF; the tablet cycles through them.
Raster line $E3: chains to raster_bottom at $F1 and, unless the tablet is open, sets the lower panel's sprite colours and multicolour (panel_lower).

Lower panel sprites: multicolour for sprites 2, 3, 6 and 7, colours of sprites 2-4 (sprite 4's from the operand at $25CF); while $1213 is zero, blanks sprites 1-3 (pointer $0F), else waits and sets $D026 from $25F3.
Operand of the LDA at $25CE: sprite 4's colour in the lower panel, animated by panel_colours.
Two values for $D026 chosen by $1213.

Raster line $F1, the bottom of the frame: chains to raster_top at line 0, raises the frame flag $120D (unless the scroll amount is 8), sets extended colour mode for the border area, draws the player's sprites (sprites_player) and saves the objects' positions (objects_save_positions), clears extended colour mode. Then handles the pause: RUN/STOP with the joystick centred pauses (scroll and speed saved, $123D set), any joystick movement resumes. Flips each object's flash colour ($C11D by $C0FF) and finishes with the scroll update.
Operand of the LDA at $2685: the scroll amount saved when the game was paused, restored when it resumes.

Copies the next six band colours of each of the three registers from the level's tables at $8B97, $8BBB and $8BDF (from index $1276) into $12BD-$12CE: a change of sky colours, triggered by a map column command.
Sets the sprite routines of bands 2-5 (the JSR operands at $23EE, $2418, $2442 and $246C) from the level's band table at $8C03 (from index $1275), each entry an index into the routine table at $12CF.

Coarse scroll step, run when the interrupt has requested one. Every fourth step it moves the map on a column ($1273): past the level's end ($8B95) it sets $1216 and wakes objects waiting for the end; a map column with bit 7 set in the level's column command table ($8715) is a command (bit 6: new sky colours, else new band routines) and is skipped. For the six rows of the map (pointers at $8709) it looks up the column's tile and sets the zero-page pointers $C6-$D1 to its character data ($B000/$B060). Each step then draws the tiles' next character column.

Draws one column of the playfield: for each of the six tile rows, four characters from the tile data, each written into both screens ($4400 and $4800, at the column $120F) with its colour from the level's character colour table at $8609 into colour RAM. When the column counter reaches 39 it first flips the screen shown ($23BE, $120C) and shifts colour RAM left one character, and afterwards copies column 38 into column 38 of the other rows (scroll_finish_column) and sets the skip flag $1210.
When the screens flip, rewrites the last column ($26) of colour RAM from the characters on the shown screen, through the colour table at $8609, for the 24 rows, and sets the frame skip flag $1210.
Stores A through the colour RAM pointer $3E.
Stores A through both screen pointers $39 and $3B, moves the three pointers ($39, $3B, $3E) down one row (40 bytes) and steps the tile data index $40 by four.
High bytes of the two screens, $48 and $44, indexed by the screen flag $120C.
Copies the objects' positions ($C25F-$C27C) to $C14A and their collision group bits ($C25B, without the low two bits) to $C00A, so the next frame's tests see where everything was drawn.

Sets the player's sprites: sprite 0 (Clyde) from $1281/$1282 (position), $1287 (pointer) and $128A (colour); sprites 1 and 2 from $1290-$1293, $128D and $128F, $1295 and $1297; the position high bits from $1241, $1259 and $125B; enables all eight.

Animates a status panel sprite at random intervals, on alternate frames. Between animations $1298 holds a delay of 6 or more drawn from the pseudo-random byte $129E (times 5, plus $81, exclusive-or $10); while it counts the last six steps, step X (0-5, kept in the operand at $2A64) copies frame X's graphics, through panel_anim_lo/hi, into the sprite data at $538F. Every 60 steps the counter $123B wraps and $123C goes up (to 3), changing another part of the graphic (panel_anim_stage) with sound effect request 1. $1227 stops it.
Operand of the LDX at $2A63: the animation step, 0-5.
Sets stage X of the panel sprite's second graphic by copying two-byte pieces from panel_stage_gfx into the sprite data at $53A7.
Graphics for panel_anim_stage, two-byte pieces per stage.
Low bytes of the addresses of the six animation frames.
High bytes of the addresses of the six animation frames.
The panel animation's four distinct frames, 14 bytes each (two bytes for each of seven sprite rows); panel_anim_lo/hi play them in the order 4, 3, 2, 1, 2, 3.

Clyde's vertical speed in pixels per frame through a jump, indexed by the jump phase $122E (0-28): small steps near the top of the arc, rising to 8 by the end of a fall. Rising subtracts them, falling adds them.
Added to a screen address's high byte for the screen being drawn: 4 or 0, indexed by the screen flag $120C.
Columns added to Clyde's screen column when his sprite's position high bit is set ($1D, $1D, $1D, $20 by the low bits of his x position); the four bytes after it are not read.
Swaps 64 bytes (one sprite's shape) between the addresses in $53/$54 and $55/$56 and moves both pointers on 64 bytes: one step of exchanging the score panel's sprite shapes with the weapons tablet's.

Counts down $12A4 while the tablet's shapes are swapped in (tablet_swap_step each frame); when done, sets the tablet-open flag $124A to $FF, enables its sprites ($24AC, $24F0), sets Clyde's colour byte $128A to $FA and requests sound effects 2 and 3.

Works out which screen character Clyde stands in: row $1284 from his y position ($1282 minus $32, over 8), column $1283 from his x position less the fine scroll (adding msb_column_offset when his high bit is set) and, unless $126C, the VSP column ($120F), wrapping at 40 onto the next row. Leaves the character's address on the shown screen in $8A/$8B.
Operand of the ADC at $2BB8: the VSP column offset ($120F minus 39) added to Clyde's column.

Clyde's movement, once a frame. Reads the joystick. Down with fire opens the weapons tablet when he is on the ground and nothing blocks it ($1235, $123F, a jump in progress): the scroll stops and tablet_open runs on following frames. Finds his screen cell and calls the level's player routine (operand at $2C32). Up starts a jump ($122C, sound effect request 4). Left and right move him one pixel unless a character at or above the level's first solid character ($8B96) is in the way; walking right past his limit ($2E5B) starts the landscape scrolling at one pixel a frame instead, until the level's end. Then the jump: rising through jump_steps, falling when there is no solid character below his feet, and landing on the row's height from $2E5E with sound effect request 5. The level's routine at $2D76 is called while $122B is set.
JMP whose operand ($2C32) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEA: the level's routine for the player, run each frame from player_control unless $126C is set.
Operand of the CMP at $2D36: the x position at which Clyde stops and the landscape scrolls instead, from $2E5B.
JMP whose operand ($2D76) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEC, taken while $122B is set.
Snaps Clyde to the height of the row he is in ($2E5E by $1284) and, if he moved, requests sound effect 5.
Clyde's rightmost x position before the landscape scrolls, by his position high bit: $C8, or $3B beyond 255.
Clyde's leftmost x position, $1F.
The sprite y position that stands Clyde on each screen row: $35 upwards in steps of 8, 22 rows.
Offsets added to the walking frame base for the eight steps of Clyde's walk: 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.
Clyde's step in walk_cycle (0-7), counted down every fourth frame by player_animate.
Sprite pointer of Clyde's first walking frame for the way he faces, from jump_frames.
Clyde's sprite pointer while jumping or falling, facing right ($49) and left ($44); also the walking frames' base.
Clyde's sprite pointer standing still, facing right ($42) and left ($40).

Chooses Clyde's sprite frame: the level's routine (operand at $2E88) while $122B is set; the jump frame in the air; the standing frame when still, and once the idle count $1230 runs out the front-facing frame $4E, resetting that face's expression to its first stage ($AEE4 with $4C); the walking cycle (walk_cycle, every fourth frame) when moving. Then, unless $1242, moves his shots and flame (the loop at $2F10).
JMP whose operand ($2E88) game_new fills from the level's hook table at $8CEE, taken while $122B is set.

Moves Clyde's two shots (X = 2 and 0, sprites 1 and 2) or his flame. A shot (state $1235 positive) follows its weapon's path (shot_path) unless $124D says otherwise, and is removed when it hits a solid character (shot_hits_wall), finishes its path ($1249), or leaves the screen (above y $33, below $3045, or past the edges); removing one frees its sprite (pointer $0F) and lowers the count $123F. The flame (state negative) is drawn at flame_draw.

Clyde's flame breath: places sprites 1 and 2 beside his head, on the side he faces, with frames from the tables at $AF32/$AF4E (facing left) or $AF02/$AF1A (facing right) for each of its 24 frames ($1238), and holds him in the breathing pose; when the count ends, flame_end.
Sets the position high bits of sprites 1 and 2 for a flame beyond x 255.
Ends the flame: clears both shot states, the charge, the shot count and the hit flags, and blanks sprites 1 and 2.
The lowest y a shot may reach ($BF) before it is removed.

Moves shot X one step along its weapon's two path scripts, one for x (through the operand at $305B) and one for y ($30BC), with read positions $1245,X and $1246,X. A byte of 0 holds still for the frame, $FD marks the path finished ($1249,X), $FE repeats the step before, $FF restarts the script from its second byte; otherwise bit 7 means backwards and the low seven bits are the pixels to move. For a shot fired facing left the x direction is mirrored by turning the BPL at $3081 into a BMI.
Operand of the LDA at $305A (two bytes): the address of the current weapon's x path script, set by weapon_setup.
Opcode of the branch at $3081, rewritten by shot_path: BPL ($10) for a shot fired right, BMI ($30) for one fired left.
Operand of the SBC at $308C: the step of a backward x move.
Operand of the ADC at $30A8: the step of a forward x move.
Operand of the LDA at $30BB (two bytes): the address of the current weapon's y path script, set by weapon_setup.
Operand of the SBC at $30EC: the step of an upward move.
Operand of the ADC at $30FC: the step of a downward move.

Sets up weapon X at grade Y: the addresses of its x and y path scripts ($B574/$B57C and $B584/$B58C into shot_path's operands), whether its shots ignore the path ($B411 into $124D), and its shot colour from the grade (through $B419 and the colour table at $CED6 into $CED5), with the grade plus one in $129D.
Finds the screen character under shot X (as player_find_cell does for Clyde) and sets $129A,X when it is solid (at or above the level's $8B96).
Operand of the ADC at $3189: the VSP column offset added to the shot's column.

The fire button. While fire is held Clyde takes his throwing pose and, if a shot sprite is free (fewer than two shots, $123F), a charge starts ($1231, $1236 counting up to 36 frames, sound effect request 6); a full charge flashes his colour (player_charge). When fire is released: after a full charge with no shots in the air, he breathes the flame (24 frames, both shot sprites, sound effect requests 7 and 8); otherwise a shot leaves from beside him in the direction he faces, with the sprite from $3306/$3308 and the weapon's colour $CED5, and sound effect requests 9 and 10.
Counts the fire button's charge $1236 up to 36; while it is full (and $129F and $128A allow), Clyde's colour cycles through the eight colours at $32FE every other frame ($125C).
The eight colours Clyde flashes through while a flame is charged.
Sprite pointers of a shot: $81 and $83 fired right (low and high), $82 and $84 fired left.
memory_swap's table of page counts minus one, for swaps 0-10; swap_from ($3315) and swap_to ($3320) follow.
High bytes of the first block of each memory_swap: $F2, $D8, $E0, $A0, $50, $50, $58, $58, $9A, $E0, $16.
High bytes of the second block of each memory_swap: $40, $58, $7B, $60, $58, $D0, $D0, $E0, $E0, $60, $60.

Exchanges two blocks of memory, whole pages, with all RAM visible ($01 = $24): swap X (0-10) takes its page count, first and second block from swap_pages, swap_from and swap_to. 0 exchanges the drive code page at $4000 with $F200; 1 $D800 with $5800 (8 pages); 4 $5000 with $5800; 5 $5000 with $D000; 6 $5800 with $D000; 7 $5800 with $E000 (18 pages, the file 1@ into the engine's code block); 8 $9A00 with $E000 (18 pages, the second level's replacement block); 2, 3, 9 and 10 the others in the tables. Ends with RAM and I/O banked in ($01 = $35).
Operand of the LDA at $3347: the first block's page, from swap_from.
Operand of the LDA at $334B: the second block's page, from swap_to.
Operand of the LDX at $334F: the number of pages minus one, from swap_pages.

Prints text string Y on the screen at the address A (high) X (low), the string's address taken from print_at_lo/hi ($33B9/$33CF). Converts the text's ASCII as it goes: space becomes character $FF; digits, '-', '.', ',' and the apostrophe are kept; letters lose $40 (so 'A' is screen code 1). Stops at a byte with bit 7 set.
Operand of the LDA at $337E (two bytes, $337F/$3380): the address of the string being printed.
Operand of the STA at $33B2 (two bytes, $33B3/$33B4): the screen address being printed to.

Low bytes of the addresses of print_at's 22 strings: 1 "COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES", 2 "FOR MAGIC POTIONS", 12 "LOADING:", 13 "INSERT SIDE B AND", 14 "PRESS FIRE TO START", 15-21 the title's lines ("CLYDE RADCLIFFE EXTERMINATES ALL" to "COPYRIGHT THALAMUS 1990"); 0 and 3 point into the level's data at $8C87 and $8CB0, and 4-11 are unused zeros.
High bytes of the addresses of print_at's strings.

Prints string Y in the big two-by-two letters at the screen address A (high) X (low), the string's address from print_big_lo/hi. Each letter is four characters from big_font (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right), one or two columns wide: space advances one column, '.' and ',' have their own shapes, digits are shifted to theirs, I is narrow and M and W take an extra column (character $28 or $29). Ends at $FF.
Operand of the LDA at $3401 (two bytes): the address of the big string being printed.
Operand of the ADC at $347F: how many columns the screen address moves on after a big letter (1 or 2), written at $3411 and $3456.
Operand of the LDA at $3489: an extra column for the wide letters M ($01) and W ($FF), zero otherwise.
Operand of the LDY at $3497: the position in the big string.
Stores A at the screen address in the operand at $349F plus Y, and moves Y on.
Operand of the STA at $349E (two bytes, $349F/$34A0): the screen address of the current big letter, moved on two columns per letter.

Low bytes of the addresses of print_big's 19 strings: 0 "GET  READY", 4 "TODAYS TOP HEROS", 15 "LOADING   . ", 16 "GAME OVER", 17 "YOU'RE IN THE TOP 8", 18 "....", others in the level's data ($8C7D, $ABF3, $ABF5) or the high-score area ($C9E0, $C9E8); 5-12 are unused.
High bytes of the addresses of print_big's strings.
"GET  READY", the big text of the Get Ready screen, ended by $FF.
"COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES" and, at $34F4, "FOR MAGIC POTIONS": the Get Ready screen's two lines, each ended by $FF.
The big letters' shapes: four character codes per letter (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right), from A, used by print_big.
Colour ramps (black through the greys and colours and back) used by the screens' raster colour bars; colour_bar_delays ($35D6) and colour_bar_colours ($35E6) are read by colour_bars.
Delay counts, one per line of the Get Ready screen's colour bar.
The 16 background colours of the Get Ready screen's colour bar.
Raster routine: changes the background colour sixteen times down the screen (colour_bar_colours), waiting the counts in colour_bar_delays between them; returns line $4A and the next routine $3925.
Sets the music player for a full tune: all three voices (A = 0), all registers but the volume copied ($17 down to 0).
Sets the music player for a full tune: all three voices, all 25 registers copied ($18 down to 0).
Clears the three sprite shapes at $4340-$43FF.
Prints "GET  READY" in big letters at $4523.
Restores the KERNAL's interrupt exit in irq_install, then installs the raster chain with $01 = $36 and the first routine at $389B, through the KERNAL's vector (carry clear).

The Get Ready screen, before each level and after each lost life. Blanks the screen, resets the scroll, the panel ($B7C0, $B840, $B8D1) and the sprites, fills six rows from $45B8 with the level's backdrop character ($8D55), swaps the Get Ready characters in (memory_swap 6, $CF82, swap 3), prints "GET  READY" and the stage's name (print_big string 1 from the level's data), the level's lines (print_at strings 0 and 3) and "COLLECT THE FOLLOWING CREATURES" / "FOR MAGIC POTIONS", and draws the music icon. Then sets the level section $1274 up from the level's section tables: the scroll position ($8C29), the Get Ready strip ($8C35, $8C3B), the three potion creatures' sprites ($8C41, $8C47), sky colours and band routines ($8C4D, $8C59, $8C53), Clyde's start ($8C5F, $8C65 into $1A9B and $1AA0) and the spawn list ($8C6B, $8C71, $8C77). Turns the music option off, starts the Get Ready tune (at $B97F, all voices) with the volume at 15, and installs the screen's raster chain ($389B).
Operand of the LDA at $37A6: the music option at the last Get Ready screen, written at $3895.

The Get Ready screen's frame loop: plays the tune with the volume $12B3 (fading), and waits for fire. Fire starts the fade-out ($12B1); a long wait without fire ($1211 reaching 50) also fades. When the volume reaches zero the screen is blanked, the Get Ready characters are swapped out again (memory_swap 3 and 6), the sound is silenced, the music option chosen ($12B4) is kept in the operand at $37A7 and the level starts at stage_start.

The Get Ready screen's first raster routine (line $FA): steps the volume fade, sets the character set and 38-column mode, animates the potion creatures' sprites when the strip has stopped ($1216: shapes from $C904, $C90C and $C914 into $4340, rotated by rotate_bytes, colours from $BF1F), counts the half-second flash of the screen ($C8, $1211), scrolls the strip (get_ready_strip) and chains to $3925 (or $3612).
Operand of the LDA at $38A8: the fade speed of the Get Ready tune, the frames between volume steps ($FF, 1 after fire, or $0C).
Opcode of the instruction at $390F, flipped between CLC ($18) and SEC ($38) twice a second, so that the next interrupt alternates between the colour bars at $3925 and $3612.
Raster routine: eight lines of background colours from $35F6 with delays from $35DE, then chains to $393D at line $5A.
Raster routine: a second colour bar, then places the three potion creatures' sprites (x from the operand at $394F, y from $395E, pointer $0D) and chains to $39A2 at line $69.
Operand of the LDX at $394E: the potion creatures' first x position, from the level's table at $8C41.
Operand of the LDA at $395D: the potion creatures' y position, from the level's table at $8C47.
Sixteen lines of background colours from $35BE with delays from $35D6.
Every third call, rotates byte lists 0 (left) and 1 (right) with rotate_bytes.

Raster routine at the top of the landscape strip: a colour bar, then the strip's fine scroll ($1240) and the level's three colours ($8CF4, $8CF2, $8CF3); raises the frame flag $120D and chains to $39D6 at line $89.
Raster routine at line $89: switches to the character set at $D018 = $19 and chains to $39E7 at line $B9.
Raster routine at line $B9: switches back to $D018 = $17 and chains to $39F8 at line $C1.
Raster routine at line $C1: clears the fine scroll, an eight-line colour bar from $35FE, and chains to $3A1D at line $D2.

Raster routine at line $D2: a colour bar, then the three sprites at the bottom (colours from the level's $8CD9 and pointers from $CEDD, stepping every ten frames through three sets), the flashing background colour from $3606, and the music option: joystick left turns it off, right turns it on ($12B4), shown by the icon characters at $47E4 ($EC/$ED off, $EE/$EF on). Chains back to raster_ready_top at line $FA.

Scrolls the Get Ready screen's landscape strip two pixels a frame until it has run its course ($C6 reaching $FF, then $1216 is set). At each whole character it shifts the strip's six rows ($45B8-$46A7 and their colour RAM) left and draws the next column at the right from the level's six map rows ($8715, $87D5, $8895, $8955, $8A15, $8AD5 at column $3BB1), each map byte used directly as a character with its colour from the level's table at $8CF5: a miniature of the level, one character per tile. Columns flagged as commands (bit 7 in the first row) are skipped.
Operand of the SBC at $3AE9: the strip's scroll speed, from the level's table at $8C3B.
Operand of the CMP at $3AFD: the number of columns the strip runs for, from the level's table at $8C35.
The map column the Get Ready strip draws next.

Rotates byte list X by one place, left with carry set and right with it clear. Each list's address and length come from the tables at $BEF8, $BF05 and $BF12; used to cycle colours and the creatures' shapes.

Sets the horizontal bounds of a box around Clyde for the collision tests: $3F = x + 16 and $40 = x - 15, with their high bits in $3D and $3E. Returns Y = $D0, or $F0 when his position high bit is set.
Sets the vertical bounds of the box around Clyde: $3B = y + 15 and $3C = y - 15.

Tests Clyde against the objects: points object_collisions' handler ($13CE/$13CF) at player_hit_object, takes the box around Clyde from player_box_x ($13BE, $44) and player_box_y, and jumps to object_collisions. Called each frame from game_frame.
Writes 5 into the flag in $B96B named by the touched object's spawn record ($C21F, from record byte 13), so that object_spawn does not spawn it again.
Requests sound effects 11 and 27, the sound of a pickup.

Handler for an object touching Clyde (X = its slot). The engine tells objects apart by the sprite frame they show ($C16A). Frames $B6-$BB are the Magic Potion Creatures: the touched one adds 1 (5 if its sprite is double height, $C006) to the counter of its kind ($B8A0-$B8A2, through $CECF) and to the total at $B89F, is removed, and is marked taken. Frame $4E (Clyde's face) is an extra life: lives ($B7BF) plus one, a fresh spell of invulnerability ($CEEB), the panel's lives digit redrawn ($B7C0). Other frames are checked against the stage ($12A2): in world 1 frames $88-$8A and $CD carry Clyde (player_carried) and frames $E5-$E9 are harmless; in world 2 frames $85-$88 call the level's routine at $A302; in world 3 the five frames listed at $A300 are harmless and frame $8F calls the level's routine at $A305. Anything else hurts Clyde (player_hurt).
Operand of the LDY at $3C83, written at $3C6D with the Magic Potion Creature's frame minus $B6 (0-5), which picks its counter from potion_counters.

Clyde touched something deadly. Nothing happens while the invulnerability timer $129F runs (unless $1215 is set) or while the weapons tablet is closing ($24F0 = 0). Otherwise it counts the death in $1214 and $1254, stops Clyde and the scroll ($1270, $22FB, $1DE5) when not in a torture chamber ($126C), starts the dying animation ($AEEF) and, unless this was Clyde's last life ($12A0) or the object is marked by $AC7E as one that survives, destroys the object that hit him ($AC7D).
World 2's check (stages 4 and 5): sprite frames $85-$88 hand over to the level's own routine at $A302; anything else hurts Clyde.
World 1's check (stages 1 to 3): frame $CD and the eight frames in carrier_frames are not deadly; of those, frames below $E5 carry Clyde unless he is already carried ($1255); anything else hurts him.
Sets Clyde's walking step (the ADC operand $2D35) and the scroll speed written at $2D44 to X: 1 normally (game_new), 2 while he is carried.
The eight sprite frames player_hit_world1 treats as not deadly: $88, $89 and $8A (objects that carry Clyde) and $E5-$E9 (which do nothing to him).

Clyde is caught up by object X: records it in $12B0, clears its $C360 and $1259, sets the carried flag $1255, doubles Clyde's and the scroll's speed (player_set_speed with 2), sets $1295 to 12 and resets the front-facing face's expression ($AEE4 with $4C).

Tables read by the levels' own code while Clyde is carried (in level 1-1 at $A4E9-$A4F5), indexed by his facing ($122D): $3D77 gives his sprite pointer ($1287), $3D79 whether he keeps it, $3D7B the shot type ($128D). The rest of the 35 bytes to $3D99 are not read by any code found.

Sets up the box tested around one of Clyde's shots (X): for a shot type ($128D) below $81 a box of 18 by 20 lines (at $3DCE/$3DDA and $3E24/$3E25), otherwise 9 or 10 wide and 4 or 17 high depending on the type. The horizontal limits come from the shot's x position $1290,X; returns Y=$D0 or, for a shot still moving ($1259,X), $F0, as the mask of objects to test.
Operand of the ADC at $3DCD: half the shot box's width to the right, set by shot_box (18 for small shots, 9 for others).
Operand of the SBC at $3DD9: half the shot box's width to the left, set by shot_box (18 for small shots, 10 for others).
Sets the shot box's vertical limits $3B and $3C from the shot's y position $1291,X plus $3E24 and minus $3E25.

Tests one of Clyde's shots (X) against the objects: points object_collisions' handler at shot_hit_object, builds the box (shot_box, shot_box_y) and runs object_collisions. A shot of type $0F (none) is skipped. Called twice a frame from game_frame, once for each shot.
Lines below the shot's y position that the shot box reaches, set by shot_box (20, 4 or 17).
Lines above the shot's y position that the shot box reaches, set by shot_box (38 for small shots, 21 for others).
Kills object X and, if it belongs to a linked group ($C3AB), every other active object of that group whose $C3AB matches (the comparisons at $3E36 and $3E44 are rewritten with X and the group).
Operand of the CPX at $3E36, written at $3E31 with the slot first killed, so the loop does not kill it twice.
Operand of the CMP at $3E44, written at $3E2E with the linked group number of the object killed first.
Requests sound effects 16 and 17, the sound of a creature destroyed.

Handler for a shot touching object X. Objects showing the blank sprite $0F, dying (state 3 or more) or switched off are ignored, as is sprite frame $8E from stage 7 on. Records the hit ($CEC2), then: hit points ($C1F2) of $FF make the object unharmed, flashing only. Otherwise the damage is $129D (the weapon's strength), or 1 when the fire button had been charged for 36 frames or more ($1236); hit points falling below zero kill it and its linked group (object_kill_linked, sfx_kill). A survivor counts the damage in $C201 towards its threshold $C210 (unless $C201 is $FF); reaching it resets the count from $C1E3 and runs the behaviour in $C1D4: bits 0-1 = 1 jump to $CEB2, 2 run one of four special responses ($2A, $06, $12, $16), 3 jump to $BEE6; otherwise bits 2-3 ($AE42, $CEA4) and bits 4-5 ($CE60, $CE80) choose. An object still able to flash (bit 7 of $C12C) then flashes white (object_flash).
Operand of the SBC at $3E9B, written at $3E96: the damage the hit does, 1 for a charged shot or the weapon's strength $129D.
The sound-effect definitions written into sfx_request's table at $FFD2 by object_flash_one: $12 for a hit that damages, $13 for one that bounces off an unharmed object.
Flashes object X after a hit (Y=0 damaged, 1 unharmed), unless it is already flashing ($C12C positive); an object in a linked group flashes with every active object of the group.
Operand of the CMP at $3F5D, written at $3F4E with the linked group whose objects flash together.

Starts object X's hit flash: saves its colour ($C11D into $C12C) and $C0FF (into $C10E) for object_updates to restore after three frames ($C13B = 2), turns it white unless it was unharmed (Y=1), clears $C0FF, and plays sound effect 18 with the definition from flash_sounds.
Operand of the LDY at $3F6C, written at $3F46 with object_flash's Y: 0 for a damaging hit (the object turns white), 1 for an unharmed one.
For each stage of the loading screen's map, how many entries of load_route_hi/load_route_lo load_route_colour paints: 0, 8, 12, 17, 25, 31 and 36.
High bytes of the colour RAM cells ($D9xx/$DAxx) that mark the route already travelled on the loading screen's map, 36 of them, ended by zero.
Low bytes of the same colour RAM cells, paired with load_route_hi.

Paints the route travelled so far on the loading screen's map: for stage X, the first load_route_counts[X] cells listed at load_route_hi/load_route_lo get colour 10 (light red). Called from the loading screen at $F8F9.
Operand of the CPX at $AC6C, written at $AC54 with the number of map cells to paint for this stage.

Counts down the dying countdown $12A1 each frame. While it is 38 or more the object that killed Clyde keeps being destroyed ($AC7D); when it runs out, Clyde's dying flags $1214 and $1254 are cleared, $12A0 decremented and a spell of invulnerability started ($CEEB).

Destroys the object that hit Clyde, whose slot player_hit_object wrote into this LDX: with its linked group (object_kill_linked) unless $C450 is set and $C3BA clear, and plays the kill sound (sfx_kill) either way.
Operand of the LDX at $AC7D: the slot of the object that last touched Clyde, written by player_hit_object; the time-out writes $FF here.
Writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports ($DC00, $DC01), deselecting every keyboard row so that the joystick reads cleanly.
Copies the level's time limit, three digits at $8CE5-$8CE7, into the timer $B718-$B71A and draws it (timer_draw). Called at each new game and from get_ready.
The y position below which a dying Clyde has fallen out of sight, by $126C: $B8 on a level, $CD in a torture chamber.

Runs each frame while Clyde is dying ($1214). While $1254 counts up the death leap (jump_steps, 29 steps) he rises and falls; once it stops he lies still while $1288 counts down, flickering between his front-facing frames $4E and $4F below 25, and fire skips the wait once it is under 125. When the leap ends on solid ground, or he falls below death_floor, the leap finishes: a speech bubble is drawn into sprites $50/$51 (death_bubble), "GULP!" when he has fallen into the water characters listed at $A300 (world 1) or with $122B set (worlds 2), otherwise "EEEK!" or "OUCH!" by the frame counter $1219, the death tune plays and his shots are replaced by the bubble's two sprites.
Operand of the CMP at $ACFC, written at $ACF5 from death_floor: the y position at which the dying Clyde has left the screen.

Draws Clyde's exclamation into the speech-bubble sprite $50 (21 bytes at $540C, seven rows of 24 pixels) from one of the three patterns at $BFC8, $BFDD and $BFB3 (X = 0, 1 or 2), places the bubble's two sprites ($50 and $51, as shot types $128D/$128F) beside him, resets the panel animation and some of Clyde's state, silences the effects, starts the death tune (music_play with $2BBC) and its volume (music_hooks_all_vol).
Low byte of the LDA operand at $AD79, written at $AD6E from bubble_text_lo: where the exclamation's 21 bytes are read from.
High byte of the LDA operand at $AD79, written at $AD74 from bubble_text_hi.
Clyde's two front-facing frames ($4E, $4F) that player_dead alternates by the frame counter while he lies dead.
Low bytes of the three exclamations' bitmaps: EEEK! ($BFC8), OUCH! ($BFDD), GULP! ($BFB3).
High bytes of the three exclamations' bitmaps, paired with bubble_text_lo.

Four groups of eight bytes from which the fast loader builds its decoding tables at $4B00-$4B1F: for each of the eight possible readings of the serial port, the two received bits shifted into each of four positions ($A0/$50/$0A/$05, $20/$10/$02/$01, $80/$40/$08/$04 and zero).
Opens the disk drive's command channel (LISTEN to device $BA, secondary address 15) and sends "M-", the start of a memory command.

Shot response 4 (behaviour bits 2-3 = 1): switches the object to the x movement script its record named ($C2F7, record byte 12, through the level's tables at $8E2F/$8E4F), once; then the remaining bits are handled at $3F20.

Returns in A the colour for character A, from the loading screen's table: the character is looked up in the list at $FA53 and the colour taken from the same position at $FA88. Called while the loading screen is copied ($F8CF).
Operand of the LDA at $AE67, written at $AE60 with the character whose colour is wanted.
Operand of the LDA at $AE7D, written at $AE76 with the colour found, which the routine returns.

The tune that starts when the stage timer reaches 15 (music_play at $B772). Header: voice 2 starts $0009 and voice 3 $0012 bytes after $AE84; the data runs to $AEE4, a command's unused second byte that is also face_reset's first.

Resets the front-facing face (sprite $4E, which is both Clyde turned to the player and the panel's lives icon): writes A over the opcode at $AEEC, clears the step count $123B and runs panel_anim_stage with stage 0. With A = $4C that is a JMP and only the expression's stage is reset; with A = $20 it is a JSR, after which face_eyes_reset also sets the first animation frame.
The JMP (or, after face_reset writes $20, JSR) to panel_anim_stage; face_reset writes the opcode byte itself.
Sets the face sprite's animation frame 0 (the copy at $2A65 with X = 0) and clears the delay $1298 so it can animate again. Called when Clyde is hurt.
Clears the x and y positions of all eight sprites ($D000-$D00F).
Sprite frames for the first sprite of Clyde's flame facing right, four frames each for the stages of the flame (index X).
Sprite frames for the second sprite of the flame facing right.
Sprite frames for the first sprite of the flame facing left.
Sprite frames for the second sprite of the flame facing left.

Clears memory from $040A and from $400A upwards for ever (each STA's operand is incremented in place), wiping out the game. Reached only from timing_check when the time between two frames is not that of a PAL machine.
Low byte of the STA operand at $AF72, incremented after each store: memory_wipe's first pointer.
High byte of the STA operand at $AF72, incremented each page.
Low byte of the STA operand at $AF75, memory_wipe's second pointer, kept equal to $AF73.
High byte of the STA operand at $AF75, incremented each page.
Low bytes of the addresses of the level's 96 tiles: tile N's 16 bytes are at $8009 + 16 x N in the level's data, which scroll_draw_column reads for each map byte.
High bytes of the tile addresses ($80-$85), paired with tile_addr_lo.

Sets the colours of the weapons tablet's three icons ($258C-$258E) from the weapons whose sprite frames they show ($2584-$2586), cycling each by its grade (tablet_icon_colour). Called every third frame while the tablet is shown.

Returns the next colour for tablet icon X showing weapon frame A: finds the weapon in owned_weapons, takes its grade from weapon_grades and steps that grade's six-colour cycle (from grade_colour_lo/hi, position kept in $12A7,X).
Operand of the LDX at $B3FF, written at $B3E2 with the icon number (0-2), whose cycle position $12A7,X is advanced.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $B40D: the colour cycle of the weapon's grade, set from grade_colour_lo.
High byte of the LDA operand at $B40D, set from grade_colour_hi.
For each of the eight weapons, 1 if its shots ignore their path scripts ($124D): set for weapons 6 and 7.
