The grade of each weapon by its position in owned_weapons, less one (0-2), or $FF for none: a new game clears all eight and gives the first weapon grade 1 (0 here). weapon_setup turns it into the shot's colour and strength.
Low bytes of the four six-colour cycles the tablet icons flash in, by grade.
High bytes of the grade colour cycles; the cycles themselves follow at $B42D, six colours each.
Puts the weapon now in the middle of the tablet (the icon at x $AC) on the panel's weapon sprite (weapon_icon_draw).

Copies weapon Y's two 24-byte icon halves (addresses from weapon_icon_l/weapon_icon_r) into the panel sprite data at $6040/$6080 and $60E7/$6127. A torture chamber shows weapon 0's icon (loader_hand_over).
Low byte of the LDA operand at $B47E, set from weapon_icon_l_lo.
High byte of the LDA operand at $B47E, set from weapon_icon_l_hi.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $B487, set from weapon_icon_r_lo.
High byte of the LDA operand at $B487, set from weapon_icon_r_hi.
Low bytes of the eight weapons' first icon halves, which lie at $B4B4-$B573.
High bytes of the weapons' first icon halves.
Low bytes of the eight weapons' second icon halves.
High bytes of the weapons' second icon halves.
Low bytes of each weapon's x path script, written into shot_path by weapon_setup: weapons 0, 1, 3 and 4 share $B594.
High bytes of the weapons' x path scripts.
Low bytes of each weapon's y path script.
High bytes of the weapons' y path scripts.
X path of weapons 0, 1, 3 and 4: 5 pixels, then 4 pixels each frame for ever ($FE).
X path of weapon 2: 5, then speeding up from 1 to 8 pixels a frame, which it keeps.
X path of weapon 5: forward 5 pixels a frame eight times, slowing, back 2 pixels a frame eight times, then forward again, and round ($FF).
X path of weapon 6: 5, 12, 0, then 17 pixels forward and back by 16, 32 or 48, a flickering spread, then finished ($FD).
Y path of weapons 2 and 6: no vertical movement.
Y path of weapon 0: level for five frames, then falling faster and faster, from 1 to 9 pixels a frame.
Y path of weapon 4: a wave of up to three pixels a frame either way, repeating.
Y path of weapon 5: a wider wave, up to five pixels a frame either way, repeating.
Y path of weapon 1: level for twelve frames, then a slower fall to 7 pixels a frame.
Y path of weapon 3: rising faster and faster, from 1 to 9 pixels a frame (bit 7 set: upwards).
Y path of weapon 7: level for nineteen frames, then jumping up and down by up to twelve pixels, then finished.
X path of weapon 7: 5 pixels, slowing from 8 to a stop, then darting back and forth, then finished.

If the weapons tablet is open ($124A), runs its closing steps to the end at once (tablet_close_setup, then tablet_swap_step until $12A4 runs out) and sets $24F0 to $FF. Called before the Get Ready screen and the loading screen.
The stage timer shown on the panel under TIME, three decimal digits (hundreds, tens, units) counted down once a second by timer_tick; timer_reset sets them from the level's data.
The timer's tens digit, counted down by timer_tick when the units pass zero.
The timer's units digit, counted down once a second.
The timer reading, 0 1 5, at which timer_tick starts the hurry-up tune.

Counts the stage timer down once a second (every 50 frames, $12AF from 49). When it runs out, Clyde dies: $1215 is set so that invulnerability does not save him, $12A0 is cleared, $AC7E is set to $FF and player_hurt runs. At 15 seconds left, if the music is off it is switched on ($12B4, $125A, sound_set_music_mode, music_hooks_ingame) and the hurry-up tune at $AE80 started (music_play). The digits are redrawn each second (timer_draw).
Draws the timer's three digits into the panel sprite under TIME ($4127-$4129, sprite block 4, rows 13 to 20) from the digit font, through the three self-modified LDAs below.

The score's tens digit.

The Magic Potion Creatures collected, in binary-coded decimal: the total, then the counts of the three kinds at $B8A0-$B8A2 that pay for weapons in the shop. Cleared at each new game.

Adds the amount in the ADC at $B8B3 (1, or 5 for a double-height creature) to potion counter X in decimal, unless it already reads 94, and flags the panel for a redraw.

Splits the decimal byte in A into its tens digit (in X) and units digit (in A).

Low bytes of the ten digit glyphs, eight bytes each from $B91B.
High bytes of the digit glyphs (all $B9).
The panel's digits 0-9, eight rows of eight pixels each, copied into the panel sprites.
Twenty flags, one for each item a level can hold only once (named by a spawn record's byte 13); item_taken sets one, object_spawn skips the item while it is set, and a new game clears them.

The Get Ready screen's tune (music_play at $37EF). Header: voice 2 starts $006B and voice 3 $0188 bytes after $B983, where voice 1 starts; with its sections the data runs to $BC2B, a command's unused second byte that is also the first of death_tune.

The tune for a lost life (music_play at $AE03). Header: voice 2 starts $0051 and voice 3 $0084 bytes after $BC2F; the data runs to $BD00, a command's unused second byte that is also fast_loader's first.

The fast loader, copied with the rest of $BD00-$C0FF to $4800-$4BFF (copy_loader at $F907) and run there. It uploads 256 bytes of drive code from $4000 (where memory_swap 0 has placed it, from $F200) in eight "M-W" commands to the drive's $0700-$07FF and starts it with "M-E" at $07AB. It then builds the decoding tables at $4B00 (loader_nibbles), and receives bytes through $DD00 two bits at a time (load_byte), storing them from page $14D2 up to page $14D1. Every few blocks it advances the loading screen's progress bar (row $47AC) and the marker sprite at $5000 (tables $BF72-$BF83). It ends in loader_hand_over.

The receiving STA, whose operand $BD97/$BD98 (at $4897/$4898 in the copy that runs) is the load pointer: the low byte is incremented after each byte, and the high byte, set from $14D2, after each page until it reaches $14D1.
The LDX's operand; the $E000 block's BIT $BDEC at $EE4F is a skip idiom, not a reference to this byte.

Runs once the stage's file is in. Stage 0 (the file 1@) swaps it to $E000 (memory_swap 7) and goes on to load stage 1 ($14B2). Stage 2 swaps the shop block, which arrived at $9A00, with level 1.1's bytes that loading_screen parked at $E000 (memory_swap 8). Then it sets CIA 1's port directions, the sound mode, releases the keyboard, waits for raster line 0, blanks the screen, sets multicolour text and the black border, and swaps the drive code out and the sprites in (memory_swaps 5 and 0). With end_flag 0 the lives go up by one and the stage starts: a torture chamber (part digit "3") at $8051 after setting $CFED and the objects' $C24C to 2 and the panel's weapon icon, the ending (stage 10) at $7D6A, a level at $E500. With end_flag 1 (the reload after the last life) it enters at $E503.
The second page that copy_loader copies with LDA $BE00,X; here the address falls on the high byte of the JMP $14B2, not on anything of its own.

Receives one byte from the drive (run at $4965 in the copy): signals ready through $DD00, waits for the drive, avoids bad lines (raster above $31 with the low bits 2), then reads $DD00 four times, each reading's two data bits looked up in the four decoding tables at $4B00, $4B08, $4B10 and $4B18 and ORed together.

Gives object X the type Y: sets $BECF and its animation script ($8D5A/$8D92 into $C29D/$C2AC) and speed ($8DCA into $C3D8), restarts the script ($021E = $FF, $C3C9, $C3E7) and sets it running ($C360 = 1).
The type of each of the 15 objects (record byte 3, bits 0-5), which selects its movement script; type $37 marks an object the collision tests skip.
Shot response $2A: pauses the object's animation for two steps ($C324), then carries on with the remaining behaviour bits at $3F0C.
Shot response 3, for an object that animates only when hit: sets $C360 to $FF so that animate_objects runs its script again, then carries on at $3F0C.

rotate_bytes' table of thirteen byte lists: for list X, the low byte of its address here, the high byte at $BF05 and the length at $BF12. 0 and 1 colour_ramps ($35B6, $35C6, 16 each), 2 ready_bar_colours (18), 3 $CA1E (15), 4 title_row_colour (16), 5 title_bottom_colours (16), 6 heart_colours (40), 7 and 8 the attract's $E5CA and $E5DE (20 each), 9 to 12 the attract's $EA6C, $EA9C, $EACC and $EAFC (48 each).
The third page that copy_loader copies with LDA $BF00,X to $4A00; it falls inside strip_tables.
Second part of strip_tables, read by rotate_bytes with LDA $BF05,X.
Third part of strip_tables, read by rotate_bytes with LDY $BF12,X.
Colours for the Get Ready screen's colour bars (raster_ready_top at $38F0).
Sprite pointers for the Get Ready screen, copied at $37B2.

The two-character name of the stage's file, built by the loading screen: the first character from stage_file_letters ($F88F), the second "@" plus the stage number ($F8A4), giving 1@, LA, LB, TC, LD, LE, TF, LG, LH, TI and CJ.
Second character of the file name: "@" plus the stage number, written at $F8A4.
The first letter of each stage's file: "1", then "L", "L", "T" for each world, and "C" for the ending.
For each stage, the length of the loading screen's progress bar, $FF for none.
For each stage, the starting position of the progress marker on the loading screen, $FF for none.
The first page each stage's file loads to: $58 for a level's first part, $87 for its second, $6A for the ending.
The page after each stage's file ends: $AC, $9A for the second parts, $8D for the ending.
The progress bar's current length on the loading screen, set from load_bar_length and counted down by the loader.
The progress marker's position, set from load_bar_marker and advanced by the loader.
The eight single bits, $01 to $80, used to build sprite and multiplexer bit masks; $BF77 is the same table from $08, for sprites 3-7.
The bits of sprites 3 to 7 ($08-$80), one per object of a band of five.
The same bits inverted ($F7-$7F), for clearing an object's bit.
Masks keeping the low bits ($7F, $FE ... $80), used for the loading screen's progress marker.
Sets bit 4 of $D016, turning on multicolour text.
Clears bit 4 of $D016, back to hires text.
The exclamation GULP!, seven rows of three bytes, drawn into the speech bubble when Clyde drowns.
The exclamation EEEK!, seven rows of three bytes.
The exclamation OUCH!, seven rows of three bytes.
Multicolour bits of the objects' sprites, one byte for each band of five (sprites 3-7), copied to $D01C as each band is drawn.
Multicolour bits for the second band of objects (5-9), read by sprites_band2.
Multicolour bits for the third band of objects (10-14), read by sprites_band3.
Background-priority bits ($D01B) of the objects' sprites, one byte per band: a set bit draws the object behind the landscape.
Background-priority bits for the second band of objects.
Background-priority bits for the third band of objects.
Double-height bits ($D017) of the objects' sprites, one byte per band; object_collisions tests a tall object twice.
Double-height bits for the second band of objects.
Double-height bits for the third band of objects.
Ninth x bits ($D010) of the objects' sprites for each band, made from $C25B by objects_save_positions.
Ninth x bits for the second band of objects.
Ninth x bits for the third band of objects.

Puts objects 0-4 on sprites 3-7 for the top band of the screen: colour ($C11D), position ($C14A/$C14B), pointer ($C16A, into both screens' pointer bytes) for each active one, then the band's x-high, multicolour, priority and double-height bits ($C00A, $C000, $C003, $C006), with Clyde's and the shots' bits ($1286, $1218) added. Called from the raster chain.
Operand of the LDA at $C055: the value stored in $D01D, the sprites' double width. stage_start clears it; death_bubble sets 6, widening sprites 1 and 2 for the speech bubble.
The same for objects 5-9 in the middle band (tables from $C122, $C154, $C16F, $C251, and $C001, $C004, $C007, $C00B).
The same for objects 10-14 in the lowest band (tables from $C127, $C15E, $C174, $C256, and $C002, $C005, $C008, $C00C).
A value from each object's record (byte 15, high nibble), saved and cleared while the object flashes after a hit and restored afterwards; level_colours_next reads it ($268C).
Where object_flash_one keeps $C0FF during the flash, for object_colours to restore.
Each object's sprite colour, written to $D02A+ for its sprite by sprites_band1-3; set from record byte 4 or its colour cycle, and turned white during a hit flash.
Object 5's colour: sprites_band2 reads the colours of objects 5-9 from here.
Object 10's colour: sprites_band3 reads the colours of objects 10-14 from here.
$FF when the object is not flashing; during a hit flash its saved colour, restored by object_colours.
Frames left of each object's hit flash (2 at the start), counted down by object_colours.
The objects' sprite positions, x and y for each, copied from obj_xy each frame by objects_save_positions and read by the sprite bands.
The y byte of object 0's sprite position (x and y alternate from $C14A).
Sprite position of object 5, where sprites_band2 starts reading.
The y byte of object 5's sprite position.
Sprite position of object 10, where sprites_band3 starts reading.
The y byte of object 10's sprite position.

Each object's sprite frame (its sprite pointer), set by its animation script and written to both screens' pointer bytes by the sprite bands. The engine tells objects apart by it, and $0F, a blank sprite, marks a slot that is empty or removed.
Object 5's sprite frame, read by sprites_band2.
Object 10's sprite frame, read by sprites_band3.
Each object's score value (record byte 10, low nibble), used by score_add.
Loop count of each object's x movement script, for a loop command (a byte with bit 6 set).
Loop count of each object's y movement script.
The last step each object's x movement script made.
The last step each object's y movement script made.
Each object's state: 0 alive, 3 or more dying (object_kill sets 5 and counts down to 4 or 3 by its death type), 5 also for a removed object.
What a shot does to each object besides damage (record byte 7, bits 0-5), read by shot_hit_object.
The value obj_hits restarts from once the hit threshold is reached: 0, or $FF (record byte 8, bit 7) for a response that happens only once.
Each object's hit points, from the level's table at $8EAF; $FF makes it unharmed by shots.
Damage counted towards the hit threshold obj_hit_need; $FF once a one-off response has happened.
The damage after which an object's hit response runs (from the level's table at $8EDF by record byte 15).
Record byte 13 for each object: the item flag it clears in items_taken when collected, or the slot of the object it rides on (ride_parent).
Each object's lifetime from the level's table at $8EBF, counted down as the landscape scrolls (objects_scroll); $FE or more never runs out.
1 while the object's lifetime lasts; objects_scroll clears it when obj_lifetime runs out, which stops its movement and animation.
1 while each object's sprite is to be drawn; cleared when it is removed.
Object 5's shown flag, read by sprites_band2.
Object 10's shown flag, read by sprites_band3.
The ninth bit of each object's x position, five objects to a byte (bits 3-7) for the three bands; the fourth byte is cleared too.
The third band's x high bits (objects 10-14); objects_scroll also reads it at $1D5C.
Each object's position, x and y in turn for the 15 objects (y at $C260); the movement scripts and objects_scroll change it.
The y byte of object 0's position (x and y alternate from $C25F).
Cleared with the positions by objects_clear ($C6AE).
Low byte of each object's y movement script address (from the level's table at $8E6F).
High byte of each object's y movement script address (from $8E8F); 0 for none.
Low byte of each object's animation script address (the level's table $8D5A by type).
High byte of each object's animation script address ($8D92).
Low byte of each object's colour cycle list (the level's table $8E02).
High byte of each object's colour cycle list ($8E11).
The x movement script an object takes when it dies (record byte 0, high nibble).
The y movement script an object takes when it dies (record byte 10, high nibble).
The x movement script a hit switches the object to (record byte 12), cleared once used.
The y movement script a hit switches the object to (record byte 13), cleared once used.
The type a hit switches the object to (record byte 14), cleared once used.
Animation steps to skip, set to 2 by hit response $2A.
Steps the x movement script may still take: $FF runs it freely, 0 holds it; for an object that moves only when hit it starts at 0 and each hit adds one (hit response $0C).
Steps the y movement script may still take, as obj_x_steps (hit response $30 adds one).
Frames before each object starts to move and animate, from the level's table at $8ECF.
Whether each object's animation runs: 1 freely, 0 not at all, $FF for one more pass (an object that animates when hit).
1 while the object's colour cycles through its list.
1 while the object's x movement script runs; some start at 0 until a hit starts them.
1 while the object's y movement script runs.
How each object moves with the landscape (record byte 8 bits 2-3: $01, $81 or $C1), read by objects_scroll.
Each object's linked group (record byte 8 bits 4-6): objects of a group die together and flash together.
The top two bits of record byte 3; kill_attacker reads them for riding objects.
Frames to the next animation step, reloaded from obj_anim_speed.
Frames between animation steps (the level's table at $8DCA by type).
Loop count for an animation script's loop command.
Where the animation script carries on after a loop.
Frames to the next colour of the object's colour cycle.
Frames between colours of the cycle (the level's table at $8E20).
Loop count for a colour list's loop command.
Where the colour list carries on after a loop.
Record byte 11: the death type (low nibble) and death colour cycle (high nibble) object_kill gives the object.
For an object that rides on another (record byte 12 = $FE), the offsets from its parent (record byte 14); 0 otherwise.

Runs each object's two movement scripts, x then y (objects 14 down to 0). An object moves while it is alive, active, not dying, its start delay ($C351) and pause ($C324) are over and the script is on ($C37E, $C38D) with steps left ($C333, $C342). Script bytes: 0 holds still for the frame; $01-$0F move right (x) or down (y) by that many pixels (a larger value one pixel more, from the compare's carry); $80-$BF move left or up by the low nibble; $40-$7F and $C0-$FD loop back (count in the low six bits, distance in the next byte); $10 restarts the script (and repositions a riding object, ride_parent); $FE stops it; $FF plays the sound effect in the next byte (when the music is off). The x script carries into the ninth x bit. An object whose x reaches 200-219 while its x high bit is set has left the screen at the right and is removed with its group.
Operand of the LDY at $C4E5, written at $C4D8 with the script position of the sound command, restored after the sound request.
Operand of the LDX at $C4E7, written at $C4CF with the object slot, restored after the sound request.
Operand of the SBC at $C529, written with the x script's loop distance, which moves the read position back.
Operand of the LDX at $C5AC, written at $C59B with the slot of the object leaving, restored after its group is removed.
Removes object X at once: shows the blank sprite $0F, sets state 5 and clears its active and shown flags.
The y half of move_objects for object $39, from its y script ($C27F/$C28E, position $020F), with the same commands; sound effects come through definition $FFD4.
Operand of the LDY at $C61F, written at $C612: the y script position saved over the sound request.
Operand of the LDX at $C621, written at $C609: the object slot saved over the sound request.
Operand of the SBC at $C663, written with the y script's loop distance.
Empties all 15 object slots: blank sprite, positions, state, active flags and loop counts cleared.
objects_clear, then the four x high-bit bytes ($C25B) cleared. Called at each stage start.

Puts object X on the object it rides (slot obj_record_ref), offset by obj_ride: the low nibble picks an x offset from the level's table at $8EFC (bit 3 = to the left), bits 4-6 a y offset from $8F04 (bit 7 = upwards); the ninth x bit follows.

Steps the objects' animation scripts, the even slots one frame and the odd slots the next (the BEQ at $C769 is turned into BNE and back). An object animates while active, not removed (state 5 shows the blank sprite), its start delay and pause are over, it is alive and its animation is on ($C360). Every obj_anim_speed frames it reads the next byte of its script: a sprite frame, which becomes obj_frame; 0, which restarts the script; 1, which removes the object; or $40-$7F, a loop (count in the low six bits, distance back in the next byte).
The BEQ (or BNE) that picks even or odd slots; animate_objects flips its opcode after each pass.

Ends finished hit flashes (restoring colour and $C0FF when obj_flash_time runs out) and steps the colour cycles of half the objects each frame, alternating by the BEQ/BNE at $C843: every obj_cycle_speed frames the next byte of the object's colour list, a colour below $10, a restart at $10, or a loop with bit 6 set.
The BEQ (or BNE) that picks even or odd slots for the colour cycles; flipped after each pass.

No code jumps here; it follows the colour-list loop and runs only if a loop ends on a byte with bit 7 set. It appends the weapon at $259E,X to owned_weapons, counts it ($12A6), refreshes the tablet icons and their positions and resets the score ($185A).
Fills the tablet's three icon frames ($2584-$2586) from owned_weapons starting at position X, wrapping to the start at the $FF end marker, and sets the selection $12A5 to the last one.
Puts the tablet's three icons back at x positions $94, $AC and $C4.
The first of three eight-row columns of pixels drawn into sprite block 13 ($4340) on the Get Ready screen while $1216 is set (rows 13 to 20).
The second column pattern, drawn into sprite block 14 ($4380).
The third column pattern, drawn into sprite block 15 ($43C0).

Entered from the attract block's $E500, with A = 0, after level 1.1 has loaded or after a quit; its $E503 enters at $C91F with A = 1 after the last life. Switches to RAM and I/O, blanks the screen, sets multicolour and the black border, selects VIC bank 1 (vic_bank_1), clears the screen, sets 40 columns and the music hooks for full tunes, swaps the level's character set from $D000 into $5800 (memory_swap 6) and inverts it (charset_invert), and swaps $1600 and $6000 (memory_swap 10). With A = 1 it runs the attract block's $E240: the high-score check and, for a score in the eight, the name entry. Then it clears the sprites and goes on to the attract at $E771.
The LDA #$01 hidden in the BIT at $C91E: the attract block's $E503 enters here after the last life, so that the high-score check runs.
Operand of the LDA at $C950, written at $C921: 0 from level_enter, 1 from $C91F, which runs $E240.

Moves the colour waves on the title screen: on alternate frames rotates one of two colour lists (rotate_bytes with X = 11 or 12) and copies 26 colours of it, offset by two for each, into four pairs of colour RAM rows (from $D949 or $D999 downwards), so the colours run across the big letters.
A line of the high-score table as it is printed: the place digit at $C9E0, the score from $C9E3 and the name from $C9E8, each ended by $FF; "TODAYS TOP HEROS" follows.
Where hiscore_print writes the score's digits for the line being printed.
Where hiscore_print writes the name for the line being printed.
The colour the title screen gives to two text rows at $D8CD and $D8F5 ($E909).
Colours for the title screen's two bottom rows ($DB7D and $DBA5, $E440).
rotate_bytes' list 3: 15 colours.

The attract's tune, started by music_play at $E7BB. Header: voice 2 starts $004D and voice 3 $022C bytes after $CA31, where voice 1 starts; with its sections the data runs to $CE5F, whose last command's unused second byte is hit_response_10's first.
Shot response $10 (bits 4-5 = 1): switches the object to the y movement script its record named ($C306, through $8E6F/$8E8F), once, then carries on at $3F34.
Shot response $30: lets the object's y movement take one more step ($C342), then carries on at $3F34.
Shot response $12: starts the object's y movement if it was stopped ($C38D), then carries on at $3F34.
Shot response 6: starts the object's x movement if it was stopped ($C37E).
Shot response $0C: lets the object's x movement take one more step ($C333), then carries on at $3F20.
Shot response 1: changes the object to the type its record named ($C315), once, which gives it a new animation.
Marks shot $43 as used up ($129A,Y = 1) when it hits, unless the weapon's shots go through ($124D).
For each Magic Potion Creature frame $B6-$BB, which counter it adds to: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 ($B8A0-$B8A2).
The colour of Clyde's shots, set by weapon_setup from the grade.
The shot colour for each weapon grade: light red, green, light blue.
The opcodes sound_set_music_mode writes at $1041: $AD (LDA) lets the third channel play effects, $60 (RTS) leaves it to the music.
The eight sprite frames of the Get Ready screen's icons, Magic Potion Creatures ($3A5E).
Clyde's two colours while invulnerable, alternated each frame: light red and black.
Gives Clyde 127 frames of invulnerability ($129F) and starts its sound's pitch at $FA00 ($0FAA/$0FAB).

While Clyde is invulnerable ($129F counting down, his colour byte $128A not negative), flashes him between light red and black on alternate frames and lowers the pitch of sound effect 21, which it requests each time; when the time is up his colour returns to light red.
Points the VIC at bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2 and sets $D018 to $17: screen at $4400, characters at $5800.
Gives timing_check three frames' grace ($05) before it starts checking.

Called once a frame from the Get Ready and title screens' interrupts. Reads CIA 2's timer B ($DD06/$DD07, into $06/$07) and restarts it from $FFFF. After the grace frames, the reading must be $B340-$B34F, the time a PAL C64 takes for one frame (19,656 cycles) less the few the routine spends; anything else (an NTSC machine, or a game frozen and restarted) jumps to memory_wipe.
Inverts all 2 KB of the character set at $5800-$5FFF, byte by byte.
In the first world's two stages (X = stage 1 or 2), sets $51/$52 and two 16-wide ranges, $47-$48 and $49-$4A, from the tables at $CFBC; the level's code at $A9E2 uses them.
world1_ranges reads its tables from $CFBB,X with X = 1 or 2, so this byte (the RTS) is never read.
The values world1_ranges stores in $52, by stage.
The values world1_ranges stores in $47 (and $48, 15 more), by stage.
The values world1_ranges stores in $49 (and $4A, 15 more), by stage.
Set to 1 by player_reset; no code in the engine reads it.
Eight bytes cleared at a new game, the first then set to 1; no code in the engine reads them.
Set to 2 at a new game and on entering a torture chamber; no code in the engine reads it.
Incremented only by the INC at $1E25, which no path reaches.

The drive code: 256 bytes that fast_loader uploads to the 1541's $0700-$07FF (memory_swap 0 first exchanges this page with $4000, where the loader reads it) and starts at $07AB, here $F2AB. That entry takes the track and sector of the file's first block from $18/$19, where the KERNAL's OPEN left them, and queues the code at $0700 as a job ($E0) on buffer 4. The job reads each block into the drive's buffer at $0600 (DOS ROM routines $F50A and $F8E0), checks its header and checksum, and sends its bytes two bits at a time through the serial port at $1800, then follows the block's link to the next track and sector until the last block.

The witch's shop tune, which the shop block starts with music_play at $EF2F. Header: voice 2 starts $013B and voice 3 $0276 bytes after $F304, where voice 1 starts; the data, sections included, runs to $F689, and the last command's unused second byte is the first of shop_fuzzy_xy.

Inside the shop tune. The address has a label because kernal_open_file's copy of the KERNAL's OPEN calls $F3F6 at $1582, with the KERNAL ROM banked in: that call runs the ROM's routine, never these bytes.

The x and y of the eight fuzzies at the sides of the high-score table: x $28 and $34 (the sprites at $34 have their x high bit set by the attract's sprite settings, putting them at the right), four rows from y $7A to $DA, 32 lines apart. fuzzies_raster copies them to $D000-$D00F.
The two frames fuzzies_raster gives the fuzzies, $F69A to the even sprites and $F69B to the odd ones, so that neighbours in a column face opposite ways.
The frame all eight fuzzies show while the music is off: $4E, the fuzzy facing the player, or $4F as each move of title_cheat_input comes in ($F116).

Raster routine at line $60 of the high-score page. With the music on, the fuzzies' frames follow the phase timer $125A: at its end the side-on pair from $F6F5/$F6F7 swaps ($121E toggles, so the fuzzies turn round), through the first half of each phase they keep it, and through the second half they face the player ($4E); with the music off all show fuzzy_face. Places the eight sprites (fuzzy_xy), gives each its frame and colour 10 (light red; $0C after the infinite-lives cheat, through the operand at $F6E3), sets sprite set 3 ($E73D), runs colour_waves and returns to the attract's chain at $E923.
Operand of the CMP at $F6AD: half the length of the current phase (fuzzy_phase_times), written at $E857.
Operand of the LDA at $F6E2: the fuzzies' colour, 10 (light red); title_cheat_input writes 12 (mid grey) when the infinite-lives cheat is entered, and the attract's start ($E790) writes 10 again.
The side-on fuzzy frames for the even and the odd sprites: $88 and $52 (X = 0) or $52 and $88 (X = 1), at $F6F5,X and $F6F7,X.
Second half of fuzzy_side_frames, read with LDY $F6F7,X.

Redefines character $4F, whose eight bytes are at $5A78 in the character set, as eight bytes of the wipe shapes at $F0C3 ending at $F0C3+X (X = 7, 15, ... 79): a full block, then smaller and smaller diamonds, then nothing. A screen filled with character $4F changes all at once.
The length in frames of each of the 18 phases of the high-score fuzzies, read from the end ($1254 counts 17 down to 0): fourteen of 21 frames, then four of 10.
The starting x and y of sprites 0 and 1 in the attract's opening scene, copied to walker_xy by $E9CB: x 0 and $5C, both on line $CD.

The x and y of sprites 0 and 1, the two creatures that walk on in the attract's opening scene ($EE73 copies them to $D000-$D003). $EDAA moves the first right, one pixel a step, and stops both when its x reaches $7F. The second starts at x $15C (its x high bit comes from sprite set 1's $E943, 2) and walks left: $EDB5 counts $F71E down and clears the high bit when it passes zero, so it stops at x $DD.

The frames of the two walking creatures (to $47F8-$47F9 at $EE7E): a pair from the loaded level's tables at $A586 and $A577 while they walk, $D1 once they have stopped, and $0F (the blank sprite) while the fuzzies drawn in characters stand in their place.
Second walker's frame (see walker_frames).

The poses of the two fuzzies drawn in characters, a new one each time the counter $1213 runs out (21 steps), read from the end with Y = $1215 - 1 (8 down to 0): 3, 3, 0, 3, 3, 1, 3, 3, 2. The tenth byte, $F72B, is never read. Each is fuzzy_pose_draw's X; pose 3 draws nothing, so the walkers' sprites show between the drawn poses.
For each of the five poses (fuzzy_pose_draw's X), the low byte of the left fuzzy's six characters in fuzzy_chars; $F731 holds the high bytes.
High bytes of the left fuzzy's character blocks for poses 0-4.
Low bytes of the right fuzzy's character blocks for poses 0-4 (high bytes at $F73B). Poses 0 and 1 give the two fuzzies each other's blocks, so that they face each other or away.
High bytes of the right fuzzy's character blocks for poses 0-4.

The fuzzies of the attract's opening scene, drawn in characters: five blocks of six character codes, three for the top row and three for the bottom, at $F740, $F746, $F74C, $F752 (all $FF, nothing: pose 3) and $F758 (the bottom row only: pose 4, the fuzzies squashed flat by the falling logo).

A sprite shape (64 bytes) that the attract's $E729 exchanges with sprite block $88 at $6200 when the attract starts and when it ends, so that frame $88 shows a fuzzy side-on during the attract and the level's own shape otherwise.

The loading screen's heading, printed in big letters by print_big: "LOADING" and the stage as world and part ($F7A7 and $F7A9, written from loading_world_digits and loading_part_digits), then "GAME OVER" at $F7AB. Both end with $FF.
The world digit of the loading heading, written at $F85B.
The part digit of the loading heading, written at $F861; loader_hand_over reads it to tell a torture chamber (part "3").
For each stage 0-10, the world digit the loading screen shows: 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 3 3 3 4.
For each stage 0-10, the part digit the loading screen shows: 1 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1. Part 3 of each world is its torture chamber; stage 10, the ending, shows as 4.1.

Shows the loading screen and loads the stage, entered from stage_next. Acknowledges and turns off the raster interrupt. For stage 1 it draws nothing and only sets up the load ($F889): the title is still on the screen. Otherwise it blanks the screen, turns the sprites off, fills the screen with character $FC in colour 11, selects the character set at $5000 and multicolour, and brings the loading screen's character set from $D000 to $5000 with three exchanges (memory_swap 6, 4 and 6 again, keeping $5800 as it was) and the drive code to $4000 (memory_swap 0). Before stage 2 it also exchanges $9A00 and $E000 (memory_swap 8), so that level 1.1's $9A00-$ABFF sits at $E000 while LB loads over it, and loader_hand_over can swap it back. It then draws the top and bottom bands, prints "LOADING" and the stage (or "GAME OVER" when the lives byte has gone negative) in red, shuts the weapons tablet and sets the background to yellow ($D021 = 7) and the border and multicolour 1 to light blue ($D020 and $D022 = $0E).

Sets up the load of stage $12A2: the file name's first letter from stage_file_letters and its second, $40 plus the stage (1@, LA, LB, TC ...), and the first and last page from load_start_pages and load_end_pages into $14D2 and $14D1. Stage 1 goes straight to kernal_open_file. Otherwise it draws the loading picture: twelve rows of 25 characters from loading_picture at screen $4520, each character given its colour by char_colour. Then it paints the route so far (load_route_colour with X = route_progress, the number of levels started), turns on multicolour and the screen, copies the fast loader to $4800 (copy_loader) and opens the file.
Operand of the LDX at $F8F1: the loading picture's rows still to draw, counted down from 11 ($F8C6).
Copies $BD00-$C0FF (fast_loader, load_byte and their tables) to $4800-$4BFF, where they run, then jumps to kernal_open_file.
The loading screen's picture, twelve rows of 25 character codes in the loading character set; char_colour gives each character its colour from the lists at $FA53 and $FA88.
The character codes char_colour looks up (53 of them), each paired with the colour at the same place in char_colour_colours; $FC, the background character, comes first.
The colour for each character in char_colour_chars: 8 (orange) for the background, mostly 11 (dark grey) and 12, 13 and 0 for the rest.

Finds the place of the score ($B7E4-$B7E7, four decimal digits) in the high-score table, comparing it digit by digit with each of the eight scores. If it beats one (or equals one that has another below it), the scores and names from that place down move one place down (the eighth into the spare entries after each table), the score is written in, and the routine returns with carry clear and the place (0-7) in $7E and $39 (and four times it in $84). Otherwise it returns with carry set.

The high-score table's scores, eight entries of four decimal digits, one digit to a byte, highest first: 3000, 2800, 2600, 2400, 2200, 2000, 1800, 1600. The four bytes after them, $FB3E-$FB41, take the eighth score when hiscore_check pushes it out.
Where hiscore_check's copy writes each score one entry down (STA $FB22,X).

The high-score table's names, eight of four characters ($FF ends a shorter one): APEX, JAZ, STUD, ANDY, DAVE, ATFR, MTB, ZZAP. The four bytes after them, $FB62-$FB65, take the eighth name when hiscore_check pushes it out.
Where hiscore_check's copy writes each name one entry down (STA $FB46,X).
"YOU'RE IN THE TOP 8", ended by $FF: the name entry's heading.

The heart the name entry's 40 symbols are laid out on: for each of 39 steps, the direction from one symbol to the next as bits (1 right, 2 left, 4 up, 8 down, two together for a diagonal). heart_step follows it to draw the symbols, to colour them and to move the cursor.

The name entry's 40 symbols in screen codes, in order round the heart: A-Z, 0-9, '.', the apostrophe, then two signs drawn with characters $28 and $29, rub and end; a zero ends the list. The cursor stands on the symbol after the one $1220 selects, which is why name_char_from_cursor takes the next symbol's code.

40 colours that heart_step lays along the heart in colour RAM (from $D92B), ended by $FF; the list is rotate_bytes' list 6, turned every other frame so that the colours run round. Its entries 9, 18 and 27 ($FBD3, $FBDC, $FBE5) are also the attract's sprite multicolours.
Entry 9 of heart_colours: sprite multicolour 1 for the attract's logo and walkers ($EBEB).
Entry 18 of heart_colours: sprite multicolour 2 for the falling logo ($ED7F).
Entry 27 of heart_colours: sprite multicolour 2 ($EBF1).
Puts the name entry's cursor sprite on the heart's first symbol: x $AB ($1259), y $69 ($125B).
The name a new entry starts as, "...." and $FF, copied to name_buffer.
The name being entered: four characters and an $FF. The character under the cursor is written at the current position as it moves (name_char_from_cursor), so that the name shows the choice.
The top and bottom rows of the cursor's box, $1F and $FC, written into sprite block 15 at $43C0 and $43DB.
Code that nothing calls: JSR sprites_zero_positions, then A into $D01B-$D01D, $D010 and $D017.
Moves one step along the heart, by the direction bits of heart_path for step X: the screen address $39/$3A by one column or row and the cursor's x and y ($1259/$125B) by eight pixels.

The name entry's tune, started by music_play at $E312. Header: voice 2 starts $00E9 and voice 3 $0152 bytes after $FC89, where voice 1 starts; the data runs to $FED5. Nothing refers to the 42 bytes after it, $FED6-$FEFF.
Nothing reads these bytes. The label comes from the fast loader's store at $BD96, whose operand had reached $FF00 when the snapshot was taken; nothing refers to $FF00-$FF6F.
fire_pressed's memory of the fire button: zero while it is down, non-zero once it is up. The name entry sets it to $27 when it starts.
Reads the fire button on control port 2: returns A = 0 (Z set) on the first frame it is down after being up, and A non-zero otherwise.
The SID channel (0-2) each of the 29 sound effects plays on; sfx_request reads it as $FF86,X.
The priority of each of the 29 sound effects: a request starts the effect only if its priority is at least that of the channel's current one ($125D).
Priority of sound effect 6. The BIT $FFA9 at $2122 and $2131 reads it only to skip the LDA #$FF hidden in its operand bytes.

The effect definition each of the 29 sound effects plays (sfx_request's $FFC0,X, passed to sfx_start). Entries $12, $13 and $14 are rewritten before they are requested: by object_flash_one ($3F8F) and by the movement scripts' sound commands for x ($C4DD) and y ($C617).
Entry $13 of sfx_effects, written by the x movement script's sound command.
Entry $14 of sfx_effects, written by the y movement script's sound command.
The processor's NMI vector while the ROMs are out: $FF00 when the game file loads; $1941 points it at $22E7 for play.
The processor's IRQ vector while the ROMs are out, written by irq_install and by the level's raster set-up ($1939, $22DA, $236A, $238D).
